D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.state: open — found incidentally, OUTSIDE the tool denominator
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.measured:
2,162 INSERTs into loreweave_usage_billing.usage_logs have been rejected by the database and lost: 2,116 carrying request_status='failed' and 46 carrying 'cancelled'. The CHECK permits only success | provider_error | billing_rejected:
  CHECK ((request_status = ANY (ARRAY['success','provider_error','billing_rejected'])))
The table confirms it — success 71,278, billing_rejected 6,236, provider_error 395, and ZERO rows of either rejected value, because none can ever be written.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.why_it_matters: A failed or cancelled LLM request still consumed provider resources up to the point it stopped. Those rows are the usage and billing record, and every one of them is being discarded at the database with the caller none the wiser — the INSERT carries ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and the error surfaces only in the postgres log. This is the swallowed-signal class: a write that always fails, silently, at scale.
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.how_it_was_found: Not by looking for it. Postgres was recreated mid-probe during batch 24 and I read its log to find out why; the constraint violations were sitting in it. The restart itself was benign (RestartCount 0, OOMKilled false, ExitCode 0).
D-USAGE-LOG-DROPPED-FOR-FAILED-AND-CANCE.not_fixed_and_why: The fix is either to widen the CHECK or to map the writer's vocabulary onto it, and choosing between those needs to know which vocabulary is canonical — this repo already has a recorded case of turn-outcome and call-outcome being two different vocabularies that overlap only at `failed`. Guessing at a BILLING schema mid-loop is exactly the move this loop keeps punishing. Recorded with the measurement so the fix starts from evidence.

D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.state: open — found 2026-08-22, blast radius SWEPT and bounded, chokepoint fix pending
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.found: 2026-08-22, while asking whether the Postgres exhaustion could have damaged evidence already on disk
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.invariant: A snapshot that FAILED is not a snapshot. A probe that could not run must make the RUN unusable — never appear as a value the diff can compare.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.measured: store_snapshot._psql returns the STRING '__error__:<stderr>' on a non-zero exit, and _counts files it under out['__error__']. That key then flows into the run's `store` as though it were a table, and `store_diff` reports {'loreweave_composition.__error__': {'before': null, 'after': '__error__:... too many clients'}} — A DIFF, which the gate reads as the owning store having MOVED. The affected entry's wrote_count is 1 entirely because of it.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.the_second_exit_of_the_same_class: _scoped_tables filters the sentinel out and returns [] — so a failed information_schema probe produces an EMPTY snapshot that is indistinguishable from 'no tables matched'. Silent where the first is merely wrong.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.why_it_matters_in_both_directions: For a read-intent tool the phantom diff is a false 'this read WROTE to the store' failure. For a write tool an empty snapshot is a false 'nothing landed'. Either way the DATA bar — the loop's strongest assertion — is decided on a measurement that never happened.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.blast_radius: 🔴 SWEPT, not sampled: 1,581 runs across every evidence file on disk. EXACTLY ONE carries the sentinel — batch19-v4, composition_motif_link_edit, run 1 — and ZERO have an empty store.before. That tool's ledger row cites batch19-v5, a later arm, so the damaged run drove no conclusion. The evidence base is intact and this is a latent defect rather than a correction.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.cause_of_the_trigger: The stack idles at 96 of 100 Postgres connections (default max_connections, never overridden), leaving four for tooling. Raised to 300 the same day — see the infra commit. That removes the trigger; it does not remove the defect, because any failed probe takes the same path.
D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHA.fix: PENDING — raise from _psql instead of returning a sentinel, so a failed probe surfaces as a run error and the gate's existing 'LIVE clean' bar refuses the batch. Held back deliberately while a 125-run live batch was using the module.

D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-A-NON-BOOK-SCOPED-ST.invariant: A store a tool writes must be IN the snapshot, or the DATA bar's silence is not evidence.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-A-NON-BOOK-SCOPED-ST.measured: world_map_update_region was called 5/5 with its card removed and returned {'ok': true, 'result': {'region': {'name': 'The Frozen North', 'updated_at': '2026-08-22T12:05:41.632468Z'}}} — the rename LANDED — while store_diff was {}. Read from the schema: map_regions is keyed (id, map_id, name, polygon, entity_id, created_at, updated_at), map_markers by map_id, world_maps by (world_id, owner_user_id). NOT ONE carries book_id, and the snapshot sweeps exactly the tables that do.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-A-NON-BOOK-SCOPED-ST.blast_radius: The ENTIRE world/map family, for the whole loop. Every 'store unchanged' recorded for world_delete, world_map_create, world_map_delete, world_map_add_marker, world_map_update_marker, world_map_update_region and world_map_remove_region was taken from a sweep that never touched their store.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-A-NON-BOOK-SCOPED-ST.why_it_is_the_worst_shape: The DATA bar is this loop's strongest assertion — the one thing a stochastic consumer cannot talk its way past — and it was reporting a clean result for a measurement it never took. Same class as D-FAILED-SNAPSHOT-COUNTED-AS-A-STORE-CHANGE one level up: there a probe that could not run became a value; here a store that was never probed became a silence.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-A-NON-BOOK-SCOPED-ST.fix: store_snapshot._world_counts(world_id) counts world_maps, map_regions and map_markers for THE RUN'S OWN world, joined through world_maps. Scoped to the run rather than the owner: an owner-wide sweep would fold in the account's 28 unrelated worlds and destroy the attribution per-scenario fixtures exist to provide. The id comes from the fixture's own world_create.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-A-NON-BOOK-SCOPED-ST.proven_by: A/B on the same scenario and the same approval arm, only the snapshot changed. BEFORE: 3/3 called, store 'unchanged'. AFTER: 3/3 called, 'WROTE 3/3: loreweave_book.map_regions'.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-A-NON-BOOK-SCOPED-ST.what_it_does_not_fix: Every other non-book-scoped store has the same shape. user_models and the agent registry's skills are ACCOUNT-scoped, and the four tools excluded from the approval arm write to them. D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.state: fixed 2026-08-22, proven by a controlled A/B on the live path
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.found: 2026-08-22, cycle 1, by a control that REFUTED its own hypothesis
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.invariant: Presence is `in`, not truthiness. An argument that was SENT is present whatever its value.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.measured: `not args_obj.get(r)` — a truthiness test where presence was meant. The model sent {"user_model_id": "…", "value": false}, exactly right, and the check returned ["value"] because `not False` is True. The repair message then told the model to supply what it had just supplied, it retried identically, and the blank-args cap stopped the turn.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.the_control_that_found_it: 🔴 MY HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG AND THE CONTROL KILLED IT. settings_model_set_active and registry_set_skill_enabled failed 5/5 while settings_model_set_favorite — the SAME shape, a required bare boolean — passed. The obvious reading was that the model omits the boolean when the answer is FALSE ('deactivate'/'turn off' vs 'mark as a favourite'). One tool, two arms differing only in which value the sentence implies. The false arm's RECORDED ARGUMENTS carried `value: false` every time. The model was never at fault.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.worst_consequence: On one such turn the model told the author "I've deactivated Nemotron-3 Nano for you" — a FALSE CLAIM OF A WRITE, caused by a check that discarded the correct argument. It also named a real model on the account.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.blast_radius: Swept from the live catalogue: 37 required arguments across 36 tools can legitimately be falsy. 6 booleans (`false` unreachable — every 'turn off'/'deactivate'/'disable'/'unpublish' intent), 10 integers (`composition_authoring_run_accept_unit.unit_index: 0` is the FIRST unit; `expected_version: 0` is a real version), 2 numbers (`world_map_add_marker.x: 0` is the LEFT EDGE of the map — a pin could not be placed there), 19 arrays (`book_chapter_bulk_create.chapters: []` is the empty-import case this loop has OWED since batch 26).
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.proven_by:
A/B on the identical control scenario, before and after, on the real chat path:
  BEFORE  bool-true  0 'missing required', 0 cap, 5/5 cards | bool-false  4, 4, 0/5 cards
  AFTER   bool-true  0, 0, 5/5 cards                     | bool-false  0, 0, 4/5 cards
The TRUE arm is identical before and after, which is the no-bystander evidence in the same table.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.swept_for_siblings: One other truthiness site exists (`not args_obj.get('project_id')` in the project-scope gate) and is CORRECT: a project_id is a UUID string, so falsy and absent are the same thing there.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.what_it_does_not_fix: It does not make the model choose the right value, and it does not change the blank-args cap's counting. It only stops a correct answer being classified as an absence. A required STRING that is empty or whitespace is still missing — that is what the check was for — and it now catches whitespace, which the truthiness version let through.
D-FALSY-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-READ-AS-MISSIN.tests: services/chat-service/tests/test_a_falsy_required_argument_is_present.py — falsifier RED on the original (6 of 8 failed), green after. chat-service suite 3323 passed.

D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.family: The eighth instance of the non-book-scoped blind spot, and the second found in one sitting — see D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-A-NON-BOOK-SCOPED-STORE and the `worlds` row omission fixed in f9d6a7c10.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.measured: arc_template carries a NULLABLE book_id and store_snapshot sweeps BY book_id, so an account-scoped template is invisible to the DATA bar. 51 of 57 arc_template rows have book_id NULL — the blind case is the overwhelming majority, not an edge. Demonstrated live: the idempotency probe archived a real template (status went active -> archived in the table, verified by direct SQL before and after) and store_diff was `{}` on BOTH calls, so the probe reported 'STRICTLY IDEMPOTENT' and then flagged its own verdict as vacuous.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.the_tool_itself_is_honest: Worth separating from the bar that cannot see it. The two responses were exactly right: first {archived: true, already_archived: false}, second {archived: true, already_archived: true} — the second call is truthfully reported as a no-op. That is the already-fixed 'archived:true over 0 rows' defect staying fixed. What is unproven is the STORE claim, which is the only evidence the bar accepts.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.blast_radius: The whole arc-template family writes to this table: composition_arc_template_edit (create|update|archive|restore), _apply, _extract_template, _drift. For every one of them 'store unchanged' has meant nothing.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.why_not_fixed_here: It needs two things, not one. (a) a count scoped to the RUN'S OWN template rather than the owner — an owner-wide sweep folds in the account's 57 unrelated rows and destroys the attribution per-scenario fixtures exist to provide, the same argument _world_counts makes for itself. (b) the fixture must record which template it seeded, and it CANNOT today: the scenario's seed uses a FIXED code, composition_arc_extract_template collides on it and returns an error instead of a row, so there is no id to capture. That is D-SEED-FIXTURE-LEFT-ARCHIVED-BREAKS-EVERY-LATER-RUN, and the two have to be fixed together.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.consequence_for_cycle_2: composition_arc_template_edit passes LIVE 5/5 but its SHIP idempotency is UNPROVEN on this named cause, so it reads `blocked` on a cause DIFFERENT from cycle 2's invariant rather than `proven`.
D-DATA-BAR-BLIND-TO-ACCOUNT-SCOPED-ARC-T.fix_design_verified_2026_08_23:
The two halves are now specified, and the blocking half is NOT the one I assumed.

(a) PER-RUN FIXTURE — VERIFIED SAFE. `Throwaway._substitute` already handles {run_id}/{run_word} and `assert_seeded` substitutes the seed_assert QUERY too (provision.py:180), so the code and name can both be per-run. `preflight_seed_asserts` replaces any {...} with a dummy UUID and only checks SQL validity, so a placeholder in the predicate does not break the preflight. The name must go per-run as well as the code: provision.py's own comment records that 'batch 19's motifs survived across arms and collided by NAME as well as by code', and the prompt names this template by NAME.

(b) TEARDOWN — THE ACTUAL BLOCKER, AND MAKING (a) ALONE WOULD MAKE THINGS WORSE. Nothing purges arc templates: `Throwaway` has _purge_worlds and _purge_models and no equivalent here, which is why 51 of 57 rows are account-scoped debris in the first place. Give every run a UNIQUE code without a purge and each run leaks a NEW row instead of colliding on one — trading a visible failure for silent accumulation, which is the worse of the two.

So the order is: purge first, per-run fixture second, and only then is the arc-template DATA count worth adding — because until the fixture records which template is ITS OWN, a count has nothing to scope to.

(2) SCHEMA PAYLOAD — refuted: composition-arc-template-edit carries the largest advertised surface measured, 17,125 tokens, with ZERO errors, against this scenario's 13,590 with five.

But arc_template_edit ALSO armed mid-turn and ran 5/5 clean, so mid-turn arming alone is not sufficient either. I have not explained it and am not naming a cause I cannot show.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.the_control_this_needs_next:
🔴 THE CONTROL THAT WOULD REFUTE MY OWN FIX, and it has NOT been run. Every failing turn dies on the pass after cycle 2's arming widens the surface. The obvious question is therefore whether the ARMING CAUSES IT — i.e. whether db4ab33c8 introduced a regression on this scenario — and nothing measured so far separates 'the fix enabled a step that was always broken' from 'the fix broke the step'.

THE EXPERIMENT: rebuild chat-service with the missing-argument arming removed (that arm alone, leaving the dispatch-path arming untouched), run scenarios-c2-motif.json at K=5, and compare error rates. Pre-registered reading, written before it runs:
  * CLEAN without the arming  -> the arming causes it. My fix has a regression on this scenario     and the fix, not the tool, is what must change.
  * STILL ERRORING without it -> the failure predates the fix and the fix merely made the model     reach the step that triggers it. The tool stays unconcludable and the cause is elsewhere.
Note the second outcome is NOT a clean bill for the fix: before it, the model stopped early and the turn ENDED, so the author saw an honest refusal instead of a dead turn.

NOT RUN YET because it needs a chat-service rebuild and the 41-tool re-baseline is in flight against the deployed image; rebuilding underneath it would invalidate 205 runs. Queued behind it.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.the_provider_actually_says_2026_08_23:
🔴 THE PROVIDER'S REAL MESSAGE, SEEN FOR THE FIRST TIME: {"error":"Model is unloaded."}, HTTP 400 from LM Studio, hit while replaying a real turn's follow-up pass outside the batch. A moment later /api/v0/models reported the same model state=loaded. So LM Studio's JIT/TTL evicts the model between requests and a turn in flight dies on the next pass.

That is an OPERATIONAL condition — not schema shape, not context length, not concurrency, not the tool set. And it is exactly what the platform's own message erases: chat-service reports it as 'the provider reported a failure without saying why' when the provider said, in four words, precisely why. Ten hypotheses were tested against the model, the schemas, the payload, the encoding, the load and the pass count before anyone read the wire, and every one of them was avoidable.

THE DIAGNOSABILITY DEFECT IS THEREFORE THE REAL ONE, and it is a product defect rather than a harness annoyance: an author whose turn dies this way is told the same nothing. A provider failure must surface the provider's own body, the way every other refusal on this platform is required to name its cause and its next move.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.tenth_hypothesis_refuted: PASS COUNT — refuted. 'More passes span more wall-clock, so more chance of hitting an unload window' predicts a monotonic rate. Measured across every cycle-2 run grouped by pass count: 9 passes 22% (6 of 27), 12 passes 4% (1 of 23), and turns with 40, 48 and 52 passes took ZERO. There is no gradient.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.what_remains_unexplained: The CONCENTRATION. composition-motif-link-edit took 5 of 9 upstream errors across 160 cycle-2 runs while four other scenarios took none over 20 runs each. A transient eviction should be roughly uniform per request; this is not (Poisson p ~ 0.005 for 5 in one of eight scenarios). Either the eviction is not uniform in time and that scenario ran during a bad window, or something about it makes eviction more likely and none of the ten properties tested is it. Recorded as open. What is no longer open is the ARMING: the fix is not implicated by anything measured here, and a turn that dies because the provider dropped the model would have died whatever the surface held.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.recommended_operational_fix: Keep the harness model resident for the duration of a batch — LM Studio's auto-unload/TTL is the mechanism, and this is host-environment configuration rather than code. Worth doing before any further LIVE-clean chasing, because gate.py fails LIVE clean on ANY errored run and an eviction will keep costing whole batches. Not applied here: the 41-tool re-baseline is in flight and changing provider behaviour underneath it would make its runs incomparable.

D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.ttl_measured: `lms ps`: TTL 1h/1h, PARALLEL 4, context 200192 of 262144, state GENERATING during the batch. So IDLE unload cannot be the mechanism while a batch is running continuously — the countdown resets on use. The 'Model is unloaded' I saw directly was between batches, after idle. That makes idle-TTL a real but NARROW cause: it explains a first request after a quiet gap, not mid-batch losses.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.correction_the_platform_is_not_erasing_i:
🔴 MY 'THE PLATFORM ERASES FOUR WORDS' CLAIM IS WRONG, AND THIS IS THE SECOND OVER-CLAIM IN THIS ONE INVESTIGATION. provider-registry-service's responses_streamer.go already handles this deliberately, and its comment records the measurement: 'Both sources are routinely empty on LM Studio's Responses stream, and Message is omitempty, so the frame serialized to exactly {"event":"error","code":"LLM_UPSTREAM_ERROR"}. ... So say what IS known.' It tries ev.Message, falls back to ev.Response.Error.Message, and only then synthesises a sentence out of the event type, response id and status — all three actionable, none invented.

The difference is the TRANSPORT, and I conflated them. My {"error":"Model is unloaded."} came from a NON-STREAMING POST /v1/chat/completions. The turn path is the STREAMING Responses API, where LM Studio genuinely sends an error frame carrying no message at all. The platform is not discarding a body; there is no body on that path.

So the 'diagnosability defect' I named does not exist as stated, and I nearly rewrote code that is already correct and better-reasoned than my complaint. What remains true and useful is narrower: the same failure IS legible on the non-streaming endpoint, so a service that wanted a cause could ask for one — but that is a design suggestion, not a defect, and it is not this loop's to make.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.correction_wrong_endpoint_2026_08_23:
🔴 EVERY DIRECT PROBE I RAN WAS ON THE WRONG ENDPOINT. The scenario's credential has api_standard='lm_studio', which routes to the STATEFUL /v1/responses API — that is why the error text comes from responses_streamer.go at all. All my reproductions used /v1/chat/completions. So the {"error":"Model is unloaded."} I found is real, and it does NOT establish the cause of these turn failures: it was measured on a transport the turns do not use.

/v1/responses is confirmed working directly (response.created / in_progress / output_item.added frames), so the endpoint is healthy in the ordinary case. What a FAILING /v1/responses frame carries, I have not captured — and that is exactly the thing worth capturing, because responses_streamer.go's own comment says both message fields are routinely empty there.

THE STATE OF THIS DEFECT IS THEREFORE: reproducible in the harness at ~40% for one scenario (12 of 30 runs), NOT reproducible by me outside it, and NOT explained. Eleven hypotheses tested and refuted, two of my own claims about it retracted, and this is the third. Recorded as open with the count, rather than closed on the nearest plausible story.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.measured_rate:
composition-motif-link-edit, four independent arms, each removing one candidate explanation:
    5/20  cycle-2 batches (concurrency 2-3)
    3/5   concurrency 1                       -> not load
    4/5   model resident, no probing from me  -> not eviction, not my contention
    5/5   fresh provider-registry container    -> not service state
    -----
    17/35  ~49%
Thirteen hypotheses tested and refuted. The scenario is single-turn, has the FEWEST tool calls of the eight, and carries neither the largest surface nor the largest payload. Nothing measured distinguishes it from the seven that never fail.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.twelfth_hypothesis_refuted: TURN COUNT — refuted. 'A multi-turn scenario issues more requests per run, so it has more chances to fail' would explain the concentration neatly. Every one of the eight cycle-2 scenarios is SINGLE-TURN: no prior_turns, no follow_ups. The failing scenario has exactly the same number of turns as the seven that do not fail.
D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE.thirteenth_hypothesis_refuted: SERVICE STATE — refuted. provider-registry-service owns the LLM streaming path and produces this exact error text, and it was rebuilt and recreated for the declaration deployment. If the failure were state in that service, the rate would drop after a fresh container. Re-run immediately after: 5 of 5 errored, the worst arm yet.

D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.measured:
FOUR of the 315 federated tools serve an inputSchema of exactly {additionalProperties:false, type:object} with NO `properties` key — glossary_list_system_standards, settings_get_defaults, settings_get_profile, settings_list_providers. All four are zero-argument reads. VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE GATEWAY (tools/list, 315 tools), not just the cached dump.

LM Studio REJECTS each one, alone, deterministically — HTTP 400 with a precise body:
  code invalid_type, expected object, received undefined,
  path [i,'function','parameters','properties'], message 'Required'
Adding `properties: {}` makes all four accepted in a single request. That is the candidate fix and it is measured, not proposed.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.why_it_matters: The provider validates the WHOLE tools array, so one such schema 400s the entire request — the turn dies whatever tool the model wanted. The account's primary model is local (lm_studio, google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat, 200K context), which is this platform's stated target rather than a fallback.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.and_the_platform_hides_the_reason: chat-service reports this as 'upstream sent "error" with no error message ... the provider reported a failure without saying why'. The provider said exactly why. Whatever maps the failure to that message is discarding a body that names the offending tool INDEX and field — the single most actionable thing about it.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.d8_does_not_catch_it: The tool-free retry (design D8) is gated on _is_tools_unsupported, which matches only 'TOOLS_NOT_SUPPORTED'. A schema-validation 400 is not that, so it propagates and kills the turn instead of degrading to a tool-free pass.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.what_is_NOT_established: 🔴 WHY SOME TURNS SURVIVE. glossary_list_system_standards appears in the advertised set of EVERY pass of BOTH the clean and the failing runs, yet 2 of 5 completed. If the rejection were deterministic for every request carrying it, none would. So either the advertised NAME list in the agentSurface event is not what is finally SENT (the superseded gate withholds 83 legacy tools after that event, so the sent list is demonstrably narrower), or something repairs the schema on some paths. I could not settle it from outside: it needs the tool names actually sent to be logged, which needs a chat-service rebuild, and the 41-tool re-baseline is in flight against the deployed image. Recorded as open rather than smoothed over — the correlation with composition_motif_search's arming is real and unexplained, and this defect may be its cause or merely its neighbour.
D-ZERO-ARG-TOOL-SCHEMA-REJECTED-BY-THE-P.retraction_2026_08_23:
🔴 I WAS WRONG, AND THE REFUTATION IS IN THE CODE I SHOULD HAVE READ FIRST. chat-service already normalises this at the MCP->OpenAI conversion boundary. app/client/knowledge_client.py's `_normalize_tool_parameters` does `params.setdefault('properties', {})`, and its docstring names the exact tool and the exact failure: 'OpenAI-compatible providers (e.g. LM Studio) REQUIRE a `properties` object — a tool with an empty input (e.g. glossary_list_system_standards, whose Go input struct is empty) yields {"type":"object"} with no `properties`, which 400s the WHOLE request.' It is applied at BOTH conversion sites (lines 675 and 788).

So the 400 I reproduced was an ARTIFACT OF MY OWN TEST: I sent the raw MCP inputSchema out of contracts/tool-catalog-cache.json straight at LM Studio, bypassing the normaliser the real path always applies. Every measurement in the original entry is accurate — the four tools DO serve a properties-less schema, LM Studio DOES 400 on it, `properties: {}` DOES fix it — and the CONCLUSION drawn from them was still wrong, because the platform already does exactly that.

IT ALSO ANSWERS THE QUESTION I LEFT OPEN, in the opposite direction to my guess. I asked why some turns survive when glossary_list_system_standards is advertised on every pass of both clean and failing runs. The answer is that they ALL survive it: the normaliser is unconditional, so this schema has never reached the provider unrepaired and was never a candidate cause for the motif failures.

WHAT SURVIVES THE RETRACTION, and is worth keeping: chat-service still reports a provider failure as 'upstream sent "error" with no error message ... without saying why' while the provider's body is precise. That mapping is what sent eight hypotheses at the model, the schema size, the concurrency and the encoding before anyone looked at the wire — but on this evidence it is a DIAGNOSABILITY complaint, not the cause of anything measured here. D-UPSTREAM-ERROR-WITH-NO-MESSAGE remains open and unexplained; this was not it.

D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.measured: world_map_add_marker, K=5, fresh: called 5/5, and after the refusal the model calls world_map_list THIRTEEN times per run and never resolves. Cycle 2's arming is working — the refusal names world_map_list, the arming puts it on the wire, and the model walks to it — but world_map_list ITSELF requires a world_id the model does not have. The real chain is world_list -> world_map_list -> world_map_add_marker and the declaration names only the middle link.
D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.why_it_matters: Cycle 2 measured that the model walks a supplier chain exactly when it can see the supplier, and fixed reachability one link at a time. This is the case that shows one link is not always enough: a supplier can have an unmet supplier of its own, and the author sees a turn that tries thirteen times and gives up. The model's own words stay truthful throughout — 'I'm having trouble accessing your Ashfall map' — so nothing is fabricated; it simply cannot finish.
D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.candidate_fix_not_shipped: world_map_list's world_id already names world_list, so the chain IS declared end to end — what is missing is that the REFUSAL the model gets from world_map_list arms world_list only if the model calls world_map_list with a MISSING world_id rather than a guessed one. Whether the arming should follow a chain transitively is a design question, not a declaration gap, and it is not this cycle's to answer.
D-SUPPLIER-CHAIN-IS-TWO-LINKS-DEEP.consequence: world_map_add_marker's old P5-SIBLING-WINS cause is REFUTED: it no longer calls world_map_add_REGION at all. Its live cause is this chain, which belongs to P3's family.

D-EXCLUSIVITY-PROBE-BLIND-TO-THE-PLATFOR.what: `ps aux | grep fe_runner` under Git Bash does not enumerate native Windows processes. It printed 0 while two runners were live, the kill built on it was a no-op, and the empty output read as 'stopped'. D-EXCLUSIVITY-PROBE-BLIND-TO-THE-PLATFOR.fix: fe_runner refuses to start when another fe_runner is live, detecting via Win32_Process on win32, excluding its own pid, and returning [] (no signal, run permitted) when it cannot tell - so 'nothing found' can never masquerade as 'nothing there'.

D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.status: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-23, same day it was filed — the call order refutes it
D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.what_i_claimed: That when a sibling wins, the staged card does a DIFFERENT thing from what was asked — kg_add_nodes for 'record that they know each other', plan_compile for 'create the chapters' — and that one case escalated scope.
D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.why_it_is_wrong:
The card is on the LAST call in all six, with reads before it, and in five of six that last call is the PREREQUISITE of what was asked: nodes before an edge, compile before apply, the entity before the chapter link, the project before the build. The model is doing step 1 of 2, not substituting. And every scenario is approve=None, single-turn, no prior_turns, so the turn ends at that card and step 2 never happens.

kg_add_nodes is not 'nodes instead of the edge'. It is the nodes the edge needs.
D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.what_survives: Only the narrow observation already recorded against the approval card: it carries a tool NAME and args JSON and no human-readable description of the action. That was true before this defect was filed and is unaffected by its withdrawal.
D-SUBSTITUTED-CARD-DOES-A-DIFFERENT-THIN.the_lesson: I read an OUTCOME (card owned by another tool) as an INTENT (the model preferred it) without looking at the ORDER. The order was in the same records the whole time. A classification built on which tool holds the card, with no sequence, cannot tell a rival from a prerequisite — and it produced a whole new problem, P14, out of a harness artefact.

superseded_content.status: OPEN — measured, 6 tools / 30 runs, zero errors
superseded_content.what:
When a sibling wins the request, the confirm card it stages does NOT do what was asked, and in 4 of the 6 the turn produces NO TEXT AT ALL to say so. Measured from the recorded prompts and pending cards:
  'Record that Aldric Vane and Mira Solene KNOW EACH OTHER' -> card: kg_add_nodes. Approving it creates the two nodes and NOT the relationship, which was the whole request.
  'Aldric appears in this chapter — MARK WHERE he shows up' -> card: glossary_propose_entities. The occurrence link is dropped.
  'CITE where it says he climbed the black stair' -> card: glossary_extract_entities_from_doc. The citation is dropped.
  'Create the chapters — make the plan REAL' -> card: plan_compile. Nothing is created.
superseded_content.the_severe_instance: SCOPE ESCALATION, verified from source. The user asked 'IN THIS BOOK Aldric Vane should be a cartographer, not a soldier'. composition_entity_override_edit is declared 'a per-Work entity override (BOOK-LOCAL field changes on a glossary entity)', scope=book. The card staged instead was glossary_entity_set_attributes, which writes the GLOSSARY ENTITY'S OWN attribute values — it applies everywhere, not just in this book. A book-local request was staged as a global write, and the turn said nothing.
superseded_content.why_it_is_worse_than_a_miss: A miss leaves the author where they started. This hands them an approval card that reads as the answer to their request and performs a different action, sometimes at a wider scope. It is invisible to every check this loop runs on the tool under test: surfaced 5/5, errors 0/5, called 0/5.
superseded_content.not_added_to_false_statement_tools: Deliberate, and worth seeing rather than quietly deciding. That field has meant the turn SAYING something false, and 4 of these 6 turns say nothing at all. A silent card that acts more broadly than asked may well belong there — it changes the ordering rule's output if it does, so it is the owner's call and is left visible instead of being stretched by me to fit.
superseded_content.correction_what_the_author_actually_sees:
🔴 I OVERSTATED THIS AND AM NARROWING IT. My first write-up said the substituted card 'reads as the answer to their request' and left the impression the author has nothing to go on. Checked against the frontend rather than the runner's record: ToolApprovalCard renders the TOOL NAME in mono, the tool's ARGS as pretty-printed JSON when non-empty, the tier badge, and 'This write is undoable.' So the substitution IS visible in principle — an author who reads 'kg_add_nodes' and its args can see no edge is being created.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and it is the whole defect: the card carries NO human-readable description of what the tool does and NO connection to what was asked, and 4 of the 6 turns added no prose at all. So the author must infer, from a bare identifier and a JSON blob, that their request to record a RELATIONSHIP will instead create two nodes. That is a real gap and a smaller one than I first wrote.

IT ALSO NARROWS THE D-SILENT-TURN INTERACTION. That guard deliberately exempts card-bearing turns because 'the card IS the output and prose is legitimately absent'. That premise holds when the card matches the request. It is weakest exactly here — a card for a tool the request did not imply — and the exemption is why these 4 silent turns were never counted as silent.
superseded_content.candidate_fix: Put the tool's own one-line description on the approval card. The payload already carries `tool`; the frontend has no catalogue to look it up in, so the description would have to ride the pending payload. Small, testable, and it addresses the measured gap directly — but it changes the approval surface, so it is written down as a candidate rather than shipped mid-cycle.

D-SUPPLIER-RETURNS-COUNTS-NOT-THE-IDS-IT.status: OPEN — measured 2026-08-23, root cause verified in source
D-SUPPLIER-RETURNS-COUNTS-NOT-THE-IDS-IT.what: kg_add_nodes returns {nodes_created, nodes_existing, entities_seen, skipped} and NO node ids (graph_schema_tools.py:2125). The tool's own check caught it — 'they identify DIFFERENT things and can never be the same id' — which is a good message about the wrong problem. The model had nothing else to pass.
D-SUPPLIER-RETURNS-COUNTS-NOT-THE-IDS-IT.why_the_fabrication_guard_missed_it: 🔴 _invented_supplier_ids only drops a value that is NOT a UUID (plus SCREAMING_SNAKE, whitespace and placeholder tokens). '66966666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666' parses as a UUID, so every arm passes it through. A syntactically valid placeholder is invisible to a guard whose test is syntactic.

NOTE the hazard measured earlier today on settings_list_models: adding a field to a tool's output makes ai-gateway REJECT the whole response until it re-federates the schema, so this needs a restart in the same change.
D-SUPPLIER-RETURNS-COUNTS-NOT-THE-IDS-IT.fix_shipped_but_unmeasured_2026_08_23:
SHIPPED AND VERIFIED DEPLOYED, AND THE RE-RUN DID NOT EXERCISE IT. Say the second part first, because the numbers look like a win and are not attributable.

Deployed: image md5 92da000b verified equal to source, ai-gateway restarted so the changed output schema re-federates, and a live call confirms `nodes` rides the response through the gateway without the additionalProperties rejection that broke settings_list_models earlier today.

The K=5 re-run (p4-chain-fix) reads 5/5 called, the invented 66966666-... gone, real platform UUIDv7 ids in its place, and the edge landing in triage 1/5 where it was 0/5. Every one of those is TRUE and NONE of it is evidence for this fix: the projection returned `entities_seen: 0, nodes: []` on the runs inspected, so the fix had nothing to return and was never on the path. The ids the model used came from glossary_propose_entities, not from `nodes`.

WHAT THE RE-RUN DID REVEAL, which is a better diagnosis than the one it replaced: the model is passing GLOSSARY ENTITY ids where GRAPH NODE ids are required. rep3 says so exactly — 'edge endpoint(s) are not yet graph nodes: 01a02c62-...'. The two stores issue different ids for the same character, and nothing in the chain tells the model which kind it is holding. In 3 of 5 it also used ONE id for BOTH endpoints, which the tool correctly refuses.

So the fix is right and its measurement is owed. What is needed is a fixture where the glossary entities EXIST before the projection runs — entities_seen must be non-zero — or the run cannot speak to this defect at all.

D-FABRICATION-GUARD-IS-BLIND-TO-A-VALID-.what: The fabricated-runtime-owed-id guard tests SYNTAX. A repdigit UUID like '66966666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666' passes every arm and reaches the tool.
D-FABRICATION-GUARD-IS-BLIND-TO-A-VALID-.caution: A rule that rejects it needs its PRECISION measured before shipping. 'UUID version is not 7' would catch it and would also reject any legitimate v4 id from an external system; 'all hex digits identical' is high precision and tiny recall. Neither is obviously right, and this loop has already paid once for a blacklist that the very next run walked around.

D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.status: FIXED 2026-08-23 — measured, and the fix demonstrably ran
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.what:
The model passes the turn's ambient book_id as BOTH source_entity_id and target_entity_id on kg_propose_edge. Proven by identity, not inference — the run's own book_id equals the value the tool refused, in three of three inspected runs:
  rep0 book_id 01a02c60-696c-724e-bbc7-46c0d97270f2 == passed as both
  rep1 book_id 01a02c61-12bc-731d-9408-6c2e4b3e07e0 == passed as both
  rep2 book_id 01a02c61-bbfd-7821-ba26-df09189ace2a == passed as both
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.why_no_guard_catches_it: Every existing arm tests for a value that looks WRONG — not a UUID, SCREAMING_SNAKE, whitespace, a placeholder word. A book_id is a real, current, valid platform UUIDv7 that the runtime itself injected. It is the most plausible-looking wrong answer available, and it is the one the model reaches for when it needs an id it does not have.
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.the_checkable_invariant:
An argument the contract does NOT declare as context-supplied must not equal one of the turn's ambient context ids (book_id / project_id / chapter_id). The runtime KNOWS those values — it injected them — so this is an identity comparison, not a heuristic, and its precision is high: a book id is never an entity id.

Measure its RECALL before claiming it fixes this tool, and its PRECISION over the corpus before shipping — a tool that legitimately takes book_id in a non-context argument would be broken by it, and this loop has already paid twice for a rule adopted on one instance.
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.supersedes: This is the real cause of the 'both set to the same id' refusals, which I first read as a fabricated placeholder (66966666-...) and then as a glossary-vs-graph id confusion. Both readings were wrong and each looked sufficient at the time; the identity check against book_id is what settled it.
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.measured_after:
K=5 on the deployed guard (p4-ctxid), against the same fixture:
  book_id passed as BOTH endpoints   3/5 -> 0/5
  the edge actually landing in triage 1/5 -> 3/5
  kg_propose_edge called              5/5 (unchanged)

AND THE FIX PROVABLY RAN, which is the part the previous attempt could not claim: chat-service logged 'dropped non-identifier value(s)' three times in the window, so the improvement is attributable rather than coincident. The earlier supplier-chain fix was shipped and verified deployed and the run never exercised it (entities_seen: 0); that is why this one was checked against the log before being called a result.
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.still_not_proven: The edge lands 3/5, not 5/5. The tool is not concluded on this. What remains is a DIFFERENT failure in the other two runs and it has not been diagnosed — naming it would be the same mistake this defect took three tries to stop making.
D-CONTEXT-ID-SUBSTITUTED-FOR-A-DOMAIN-ID.recall_limit:
🔴 THE GUARD ONLY SEES CONTEXT IDS THE MODEL ECHOED BACK IN THE SAME CALL. It compares a suspect value against args_obj's own book_id/chapter_id/project_id. When the model passes an ambient id it did NOT also include as an argument — say chapter_id as an entity_id, with no chapter_id argument on that call — there is nothing to compare against and the guard is blind.

The runtime KNOWS those values, because it injected them, so a fuller version would compare against the turn's ambient context rather than the call's own arguments. That is a bigger change to a hot path and its precision would have to be re-measured against the corpus, since the 180-firing measurement was taken with the same-call comparison. Recorded as a known recall limit rather than quietly implied to be complete.

D-REBIND-DUPLICATES-INSTEAD-OF-ARCHIVING.status: RETRACTED 2026-08-23, within the hour, by the control I ran against my own claim
D-REBIND-DUPLICATES-INSTEAD-OF-ARCHIVING.what_i_claimed: That re-binding duplicates instead of archiving: motif_application 2->4, outline_node 3->5, archived_scene_ids empty on the second call — contradicting the tool's own 're-binding archives the prior scenes'.
D-REBIND-DUPLICATES-INSTEAD-OF-ARCHIVING.why_it_was_wrong:

I read a fixture's missing link as the tool's missing archive.

With chapter_id supplied: archived_scene_ids is POPULATED on the second call and motif_application stays at 2. The tool does exactly what it says.
D-REBIND-DUPLICATES-INSTEAD-OF-ARCHIVING.what_actually_remains: outline_node still grows 3 -> 5, and that is BY DESIGN: the archive is SOFT — `_set_scenes_archived(..., archived=True)` — because the comment says 'the prior scenes (now archived — prose preserved)'. The rows are kept on purpose so an author does not lose written prose. Growth is the archive, not a duplicate.
D-REBIND-DUPLICATES-INSTEAD-OF-ARCHIVING.the_instrument_lesson: idempotency_probe's verdict is a ROW-COUNT heuristic and it cannot tell 'duplicated' from 'soft-archived and replaced'. It printed 'NOT IDEMPOTENT' for a tool behaving correctly. That is a real limit worth knowing before the next soft-archiving tool is probed: the count is the symptom, the LIFECYCLE COLUMN is the diagnosis — see D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFECYCLE.

superseded_content.what:
composition_motif_bind_edit op=bind, called TWICE with identical arguments, DUPLICATES instead of replacing:
    loreweave_composition.motif_application   2 -> 4
    loreweave_composition.outline_node        3 -> 5
Both calls returned success:true, and the SECOND returned archived_scene_ids: [] while minting a fresh new_scene_ids pair. The chapter now carries two complete instantiations of the same motif.
superseded_content.it_contradicts_its_own_declaration: The tool's description states 'op=bind instantiates the motif's beats as scene nodes ... re-binding archives the prior scenes, reversible'. Re-binding archived nothing: archived_scene_ids was EMPTY on the second call. The promise and the behaviour disagree, and the declaration is the half an author reads.
superseded_content.why_it_was_never_seen:
Its idempotency ship case sat OWED for the whole loop because the probe could not reach the tool at all: node_id is an OUTLINE node and every seed built ARCS or used book_chapter_create, which composition-service's own source says does not mint outline_node rows. Once the fixture minted a real outline node the bind SUCCEEDED and still wrote nothing — new_scene_ids: [] — because the seeded motif had no BEATS, and 'instantiates the motif's beats' means a beatless motif is a no-op. Only with BOTH an outline node and a motif carrying beats does the tool do enough work for a second call to be able to duplicate it.

Three fixture layers deep, and the probe's own guard refused to call either earlier attempt a pass: 'STRICTLY IDEMPOTENT ... BUT THE FIRST CALL CHANGED NOTHING EITHER, so this probe measured two no-ops and proves nothing.' Without that line this would have been recorded as idempotent, twice, on empty store diffs.

D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.what: idempotency_probe decides by comparing ROW COUNTS before and after the second call. A tool that SOFT-archives the prior rows and writes replacements grows the table and is reported 'NOT IDEMPOTENT — the second call DUPLICATED', which is false: the old rows are archived, not live. composition_motif_bind_edit is the measured case.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-COUNTS-ROWS-NOT-LIFE.fix_direction: Where the table carries a lifecycle column, compare ACTIVE rows — the probe already knows the table names, and store_snapshot already reads these stores. Until then, read a growth verdict on a soft-archiving tool as a QUESTION rather than an answer.

D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-CANNOT-MEASURE-A-CON.what:

For a CONFIRM-GATED (Tier-W) tool that measures nothing: the call only MINTS a confirm_token and writes nothing until the token is redeemed, so both diffs are empty and the probe's own guard correctly says 'two no-ops ... proves nothing'.

Measured on composition_decompile_arcs. With the outline_node fixture in place it stopped answering 'no chapters to decompile' and started returning a confirm_token — real progress, and still unmeasurable by this instrument.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-CANNOT-MEASURE-A-CON.what_the_probe_would_have_to_do: call -> redeem -> call -> redeem, comparing the store across the SECOND redemption. The redemption path is already known and used by the seeds: POST /v1/{domain}/actions/confirm. This is a bounded extension, not a redesign.

Every Tier-W tool in the denominator has an idempotency case in the same position.

D-SCHEMA-WRITE-APPLIES-ON-A-SIGNATURE-TH.what:
kg_triage_schema_write accepts a `signature` that does not exist, mints a confirm token for it, and the redemption APPLIES the schema change:
    signature = 'no-such-signature-000', action = add_to_schema, code = 'probe_edge_absent'
    -> {"applied": true, "schema_version": 2, "stamped": 0, "resolved": 0}
The edge type is added to the project's ontology. `resolved: 0` is the tell — the tool knows it resolved no triage group, and applies the mutation anyway.
D-SCHEMA-WRITE-APPLIES-ON-A-SIGNATURE-TH.why_it_matters: The tool's whole contract is 'Resolve a schema-mutating triage signature group'. The signature is the AUTHORITY for the change: it says a real proposal needed this edge type. Without validating it, any caller that invents a signature can mutate a project's ontology, and the response says applied:true — so nothing downstream can tell the difference.
D-SCHEMA-WRITE-APPLIES-ON-A-SIGNATURE-TH.it_reached_the_boundary_only_after_a_pre: The first probe refused with 'this project has no adopted ontology to edit', which is a refusal arriving BEFORE the boundary — the same trap recorded for kg_propose_edge and glossary_create_chapter_link today. An ontology was adopted into the probe project first, and only then could the signature check be tested. A boundary probe that stops at the first refusal reports a guard that was never exercised.
D-SCHEMA-WRITE-APPLIES-ON-A-SIGNATURE-TH.cleanup_note: The probe added edge type 'probe_edge_absent' to the ZZ Throwaway kg_project_create probe project — my own throwaway, created for probes. Left in place rather than reverted: a schema_version bump is not obviously reversible and inventing a rollback here risks more than the debris does.

The edit was inert and the run looked like a refutation of it.

Compare it against the scenario's `prompt` before reading any result: they differ exactly when follow_ups exist. jobs_cancel/jobs_pause have none, which is why the same edit worked there — 0/5 -> 5/5.

D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.status: OPEN — PROVEN against the owning store, 2026-08-23
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.what:
memory_forget re-stamps a Fact's `valid_until` on EVERY call and reports {'invalidated': true} each time. Measured in Neo4j directly:
    before a repeat call : valid_until = 2026-08-23T07:52:12.211Z
    after                : valid_until = 2026-08-23T07:54:29.154Z
The fact was already invalidated. The second call moved WHEN it stopped being true.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.why_it_matters: valid_until is the temporal record — the moment the fact ceased to hold. Re-stamping it means a fact invalidated at 07:52 now claims it was valid until 07:54, so any as-of query in that window returns a fact the author had already retracted. This is the exact case the idempotency bar names: a second call 'must not corrupt what the first call wrote'.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.the_response_cannot_reveal_it: Both calls answer {'invalidated': true}, identical. A caller cannot tell a real invalidation from a re-stamp, and the tool DOES have a false form — an absent fact_id correctly answers {'invalidated': false, 'reason': 'no matching fact found'} — so the honest answer exists and is not used here.
D-FORGET-RESTAMPS-VALID-UNTIL-AND-REWRIT.measured_by: direct Neo4j read before/after a repeat memory_forget, 2026-08-23

D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-IS-BLIND-TO-NEO4J-OW.what: idempotency_probe compares store_snapshot before/after, and store_snapshot reads POSTGRES. For a tool whose owning store is Neo4j it therefore compares two empty pictures and reports 'STRICTLY IDEMPOTENT — the second call touched nothing at all'.
D-IDEMPOTENCY-PROBE-IS-BLIND-TO-NEO4J-OW.measured_consequence: It printed exactly that for memory_forget, which re-stamps valid_until on every call. The verdict was not merely unproven — it was the OPPOSITE of the truth, and only a direct Neo4j read found it. The probe's own '⚠ the first call changed nothing either' guard fired, which is the signal that saved it: on a Neo4j-owned tool that warning means the instrument is blind, not that the tool is quiet.

D-A-REQUIRED-ID-NO-TOOL-CAN-SUPPLY.sweep_and_its_precision:
🔴 I SWEPT FOR MORE AND THE SWEEP IS A LEAD GENERATOR, NOT A FINDING. Across the 315-tool catalogue, 12 required *_id arguments (of 40, excluding the runtime context ids) are named by NO other tool:
  attr_value_id, base_version_id, edited_from_version_id, fact_id, import_source_id, marker_id,
  provider_credential_id, reference_id, region_id, source_entity_id, task_id, triage_id

MOST OF THOSE HAVE A REAL SUPPLIER. The test only asks whether the ID NAME appears in another tool's schema or description, and a reader routinely returns the value under a different key: world_map_get returns markers and regions, kg_triage_list returns triage items, settings_list_providers returns credentials, jobs_list returns tasks. Reporting 12 defects would have been a precision failure of exactly the kind this loop measures before shipping a lint.

ONE IS VERIFIED: reference_id. There is no MCP tool that lists reference sources at all — checked by looking for a READER of the noun, not just the id name. That check is what separates a genuine orphan from a naming mismatch, and it is the check to run on the other eleven before any of them is called a defect.

D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.status: OPEN — REFRAMED by a control that already existed
D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.what:
Across all 875 recorded runs, the 'upstream sent error with no message' / ReadTimeout stall is not spread evenly. It concentrates on turns that call composition_motif_search:
    called composition_motif_search   41 runs   73% errored
    motif-family tools, NO search     16 runs    0% errored
    no motif tool at all             818 runs    6% errored
A 12x difference against the baseline, and the middle row is the control that matters: sixteen runs used composition_motif_* tools WITHOUT the search and not one errored. So it is not the motif family, the fixture, or the domain — it tracks that single tool.
D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.why_it_matters: This loop spent THIRTEEN refuted hypotheses on composition_motif_link_edit's ~49% stall — not load, not eviction, not probe contention, not service state, not turn count, not schema size, not encoding, not context pressure — and concluded the cause was not findable. Every one of those runs calls composition_motif_search, and so does every failing composition_motif_adopt run measured today (4 of 5 errored, each dying right after the search).
D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.what_it_is_NOT: Payload size. Measured directly: a targeted query returns 4,898 bytes / 20 items, and detail=full returns 12,000. That is nothing against a 200K context, so 'the result is too big' is refuted rather than assumed.
D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.not_yet_causation: 41 runs is a modest n, and the search is called precisely in the turns that need a name resolved — which are also the hardest turns. The 0% control weakens that reading but does not kill it. The next step is a DIRECT one: a scenario whose measured turn calls composition_motif_search and nothing else, at K=5. If it stalls alone, the tool is the cause.
D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.the_control_that_already_existed:
🔴 THE SEARCH ALONE DOES NOT STALL, and the evidence was already on disk before I proposed running it. composition_motif_search was measured as the TOOL UNDER TEST at K=5 — batch20-motif-search-clean.json, prompt 'Find the trope called Emberfall Reversal in my motif library' — and errored 0 of 5. My previous entry said 'the next step is a scenario whose measured turn calls composition_motif_search and nothing else; if it stalls alone, the tool is the cause'. That experiment had been run. It does not stall alone.

So the correlation is not 'this tool breaks turns'. What differs is what the turn must do NEXT: in its own scenario the search IS the answer and the model replies in prose; in every failing case the search is a SUPPLIER and the model must emit another TOOL CALL from its result.
D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.and_one_split_is_circular: 🔴 A SPLIT I ALMOST REPORTED AS A FINDING. Among runs calling the search: 'search was the LAST call' errors 81% (37 runs) and 'the turn CONTINUED after it' errors 0% (4 runs). That reads like a discovery and is largely a TAUTOLOGY — when the turn dies after the search, the search IS the last call by consequence. The error causes the classification. Recorded so nobody mines that number later as evidence.
D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.what_is_solid:
* the search as an ANSWER: 0/5 errored (its own scenario, K=5)
  * turns that must ACT on a search result: 73% errored over 41 runs
  * motif-family tools that never call the search: 0% over 16 runs
  * not payload size — a targeted query is 4,898 bytes, detail=full 12,000
The remaining hypothesis is emitting a TOOL CALL after a search result, which is the shape of the documented LM Studio parser defect the platform already records for this model — the structured tool-call channel emitting nothing while free text still works. That is testable by a scenario whose measured turn must call one tool AFTER a search, versus one that must only answer.
D-THE-STALL-CONCENTRATES-ON-COMPOSITION-.narrowed_2026_08_23:
A CONTROLLED A/B INSIDE ONE BATCH. c-adopt3, K=5, one scenario, one query: 3 runs died, 2 did not. Everything the platform sends was identical between them.

  * composition_motif_search returned 532 bytes, byte-identical, in all five runs (args identical too: {"q": "Face-Slap Reversal", "scope": "system"}). PAYLOAD REFUTED at fixed scenario, which is stronger than the earlier cross-scenario refutation.
  * provider-registry logged 'chat context preflight' for pass 1 (14402 tok) AND pass 2 (14556 tok) in ALL five runs. So the failing request IS built and IS sent — the failure is inside pass 2, the first pass after the tool result. Previously it was not known whether the request was even reaching the provider.
  * clean runs then log pass 3 (14723 tok) and a ~120-token title call; dying runs log neither.
  * input token count on the failing pass is the SAME 14556 in both populations.

SO: same input, same size, same tool result, different outcome. The failure is in GENERATION on the pass whose job is to emit the next tool call — not in anything the platform composes.

IDLE-UNLOAD TESTED AND NOT SUPPORTED. If the model were being evicted during a slow tool call, longer pass1->pass2 gaps would fail. Measured the opposite ordering: died at 5.2s, 9.5s, 15.6s; survived at 16.2s, 18.1s. n=5, so this is recorded as 'not supported', NOT as a refutation with a direction.

🔴 THE DIAGNOSIS IS CURRENTLY BLOCKED ON PROVIDER OBSERVABILITY, and that is an owner action. The provider is LM Studio at http://host.docker.internal:1234/v1 (provider_kind lm_studio, google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat, context_length 200000, credential active). Its server logs at ~/.lmstudio/server-logs have not been written since 2026-08-04 — nineteen days. D-THE-TRANSPORT-STALL-IS-THREE-DIFFERENT.status: OPEN — structural finding, 2026-08-23; it reframes the loop's biggest open question
D-THE-TRANSPORT-STALL-IS-THREE-DIFFERENT.what:
'The transport stall' has been treated as ONE phenomenon and hunted with one hypothesis at a time. Split by whether the turn emitted any tool call, and by error type, it is THREE populations across 80 errored runs:

  ZERO tool calls (42)      PROVISION seed failure  20
                            ReadTimeout             17
                            upstream error           5
  >=1 tool call   (38)      upstream error, no msg  35   <- 30 of 38 called motif_search
                            ReadTimeout              3

  1. PROVISION (20) is not the platform at all — the SEED could not build the fixture.
  2. ReadTimeout with zero calls (17) — the turn never produced anything in the budget, and raising that budget 180s -> 480s did not fix it.
  3. upstream error after >=1 call (35) — the provider fails MID-turn, and 79% of those turns had called composition_motif_search.
D-THE-TRANSPORT-STALL-IS-THREE-DIFFERENT.why_it_matters: This is why thirteen hypotheses were refuted for composition_motif_link_edit. Each was tested against a MIXED population, so a cause that explains one third looks refuted by the other two. Its own runs contain both ReadTimeout-with-no-calls and upstream-error-after-a-search, and they were counted as one number (~49%).
D-THE-TRANSPORT-STALL-IS-THREE-DIFFERENT.what_this_already_refuted:
Measured cheaply from the existing corpus, and each is a real refutation rather than an untested guess:
  payload size    a targeted motif_search returns 4,898 bytes; detail=full 12,000
  parser defect   blank-args breaker and search-stall are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — 0 overlap in 141 runs
  surface size    errored mean 32.1 hot-seed vs clean 33.8 — clean is LARGER
  context growth  errored mean 968 result bytes vs clean 2,512 — errored carry LESS
  turn length     errored median 0 tool calls vs clean 2 — errored are SHORTER
D-THE-TRANSPORT-STALL-IS-THREE-DIFFERENT.next_step: Stop measuring 'the stall'. Each population needs its own question: why a seed fails (fixture), why a turn emits nothing in 480s (population 2), and what a provider does with a search result mid-turn (population 3). A single number over all three cannot move.
