D-HARNESS-agentSurface-DISAGREES-WITH-TH.status: OPEN — INSTRUMENT DEFECT, found 2026-08-23. It invalidates a class of claim this loop has been making, including in an entry committed earlier the same day.
D-HARNESS-agentSurface-DISAGREES-WITH-TH.what:
fe_runner records every agentSurface CUSTOM event and the loop reads 'advertised in N of M snapshots' off them. chat-service ALSO logs the real per-pass wire set at INFO ('agent-surface advertised (session=…): core=… activated=[…]'). On the same two sessions they disagree:

  session 01a02e76 — wire log: 6 passes, composition_arc_apply present on 4 of them
                     harness  : 6 snapshots, composition_arc_apply present in 0
  session 01a02e77 — wire log: 5 passes, present on 4
                     harness  : 4 snapshots, present in 0

The counts differ AND the content differs. The wire log is built from the same list the chokepoint returns and hands to the provider, so it is the authority; the harness's `advertised` field is not a measurement of what the model could see.

Mechanism not yet isolated. AgentSurfaceTracker.advertised_pass() returns a payload ONLY when the set changed, while _transition() emits payload() (which embeds the stored `advertised`) on every phase change — so an ordering or a dropped-emission difference between the two is the place to look. Recorded before isolating it because the CONSEQUENCE is what matters and is already proven.
D-HARNESS-agentSurface-DISAGREES-WITH-TH.what_it_invalidates:
Every 'advertised in N of M snapshots' figure this loop has published, including the ones in D-R1-ANSWERABILITY-IS-INERT-ON-EVERY-RESUMED-TURN and in commit 577babc38. Those numbers must be re-derived from the chat-service INFO log before being cited again.

IT DOES NOT INVALIDATE THE R1 RESUME FIX, and the distinction is the point. That fix rests on two things the instrument never touched: (a) the CODE fact that resume_stream_response omitted request_text, whose default the parameter's own docstring calls inert — asserted by an AST test proven RED; and (b) the BEHAVIOURAL A/B, glossary_create_evidence called 0/5 before and 4/5 after, which is measured from tool calls, not from surfaces. A surface count was corroboration in that entry, not its evidence.
D-HARNESS-agentSurface-DISAGREES-WITH-TH.how_it_was_found: By instrumenting R1 itself. composition_arc_apply looked 'advertised 0/40' while answerable_tools picked it against the live 303-tool catalogue — an impossible pair. The new INFO line proved the rescue fires and the tool reaches the wire, and the two passes where it did NOT fire turned out to be the scenario's FOLLOW-UP turn ('Yes, go ahead and do it.'), whose text genuinely matches no tool's vocabulary. That part is correct behaviour, not a defect — recorded so it is not later mined as one.

D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-TH.status: OPEN — measured 2026-08-23 against the live 303-tool catalogue. General; it is the mechanism behind two of today's blocked diagnoses.
D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-TH.what:
_name_like_dropped_ids appends: 'the name is what you search WITH: look it up with THE TOOL NAMED ABOVE and pass the id it returns, using that exact name as the query.'

'The tool named above' means a supplier named in the TOOL'S OWN DESCRIPTION — the function's docstring is explicit about where the phrase came from: composition_motif_link_edit's description says 'search motifs by name with composition_motif_search and pass the id it returns', and the sentence was written to point at that. When a description names no tool, the model is told to use a tool that was never named, and the repair reads as a complete instruction while carrying no referent.
D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-TH.measured:
Live catalogue, 303 tools, 2026-08-23. Counting tools with at least one REQUIRED *_id argument that is a UUID and is not one of the ambient runtime ids (book_id / chapter_id / project_id), then asking whether the tool's description contains the name of any other catalogue tool:

    86  tools require a non-ambient UUID id
    41  name a supplier in their description
    45  name NO tool at all  (52%)

Among the 45: composition_arc_template_get, composition_motif_get, composition_motif_archive, composition_motif_link_list, composition_motif_link_delete, composition_motif_unbind, composition_outline_node_delete, composition_canon_rule_delete, composition_authoring_run_gate / _pause / _revert_all, composition_get_mine_job, book_chapter_restore_revision.

METHOD, stated so it can be checked: substring match of catalogue tool names against each description, and the id filter is 'required, ends in _id, and either format=uuid or "uuid" in the arg description'. It will over-count a description that merely mentions an unrelated tool, which makes 45 a LOWER bound on the problem, not an upper one.
D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-TH.seen_live: c-arcapply, K=5. The model passed arc_id='The Varisuni Ascent' — a NAME — to composition_arc_template_get, got this repair, and then called composition_arc_suggest, a guess. It never called composition_arc_template_list, which is the real supplier and which was on no pass of the wire. Its closing message to the user was 'I still can't find an arc template named "The Varisuni Ascent"' — about a template its own run had just created.
D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-TH.recommendation_for_owner: The platform holds the catalogue at the moment it writes this sentence, so it can name the supplier instead of gesturing at one. Failing that, the clause should be dropped when the description names nothing — an instruction with no referent is worse than no instruction, because the model spends its turn acting on it. NOT MY CALL; recorded for decision.
D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-TH.denominator_correction:
🔴 THE 86 UNDER-COUNTS, and the tools it misses are the ones most likely to fail. The sweep counted tools with a REQUIRED *_id argument that is a UUID. A flat-superset op-dispatch tool declares only `op` (and sometimes an ambient id) as required - every other argument is optional with default null - so composition_authoring_run_manage's plan_run_id was never in the population, even though the handler refuses without it on 4 of 5 runs. ship_probe.py's docstring counts 15 catalogue tools whose only required argument is `op` (measured 2026-08-22).

Worse for the repair specifically: those arguments carry a `title` and NO `description`, so the branch that quotes the argument's own declaration has nothing to quote and falls through to 'does not declare which side supplies them'. The tools whose requirements are invisible to the schema are also the tools the repair can say least about.

D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.status: OPEN — harness gap, found 2026-08-23. Small, but it is the kind that accumulates into the 51-of-57 test debris this loop already has to reason around.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.what:
provision.py --sweep removes throwaway BOOKS and WORLDS. It does not remove account-scoped rows a seed created — measured directly: after a --keep-fixtures run of scenarios-c-arcapply.json, --sweep reported 'swept 1 throwaway book(s) / swept 1 throwaway world(s)' and the seeded arc_template row was still there. Deleted by hand after a SELECT.

The normal per-run teardown DOES handle them: seven earlier runs of the same scenario left zero loop-arc-% rows. So the gap is exactly the --keep-fixtures path, which is the investigation path — the one taken when something has already gone wrong and nobody is watching the store.

This is also how a scenario note came to claim the opposite. The note asserted the rows persist because the book teardown cannot see them; that was reasoning from the schema rather than from the store, and the store said zero. Corrected in place.
D-HARNESS-sweep-DOES-NOT-COVER-ACCOUNT-S.affects: Any scenario whose seed writes to the caller's own library — arc templates, motifs, memories.

D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.status: OPEN — cross-cutting measurement over ALL evidence on disk, 2026-08-23. Not a new defect: it is the size of the one this loop keeps meeting tool by tool.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.what:
Swept every *-raw.json in docs/eval/toolloop for TOOL_CALL_RESULTs and classified the failures. One family — a REQUIRED ARGUMENT the model could not supply, almost always an opaque id — is the dominant failure of the entire loop. Counted in both its forms: the direct refusal ('is missing required argument(s): [...]') and the loop-breaker ('keeps being called with missing/blank required arguments').

    ALL evidence        2410 results, 1030 failed,  779 in the family = 76%, 25 tools
    EXCLUDING world_*   1693 results,  445 failed,  213 in the family = 48%, 19 tools

BOTH NUMBERS ARE GIVEN BECAUSE ONE GROUP DOMINATES THE FIRST. world_map_list alone is 317 of the 779 (41%), and the world_* family is 563 (72%) — a single tool looping inflates the headline. The honest claim is the second: with world_* set aside entirely, this is still ~half of every tool-call failure the loop has ever recorded, across 19 distinct tools.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.top_tools: world_map_list 317, world_map_create 77, world_get 66, world_map_add_marker 53, world_map_delete 50, jobs_get 39, composition_motif_link_edit 36, composition_reference_update 16, composition_motif_bind_edit 13, translation_patch_block 12.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.why_it_matters:
Four of the tools still BLOCKED carry this exact signature — composition_motif_link_edit (from_motif_id, to_motif_id), composition_reference_update (reference_id), glossary_create_evidence (attr_value_id), memory_forget (fact_id) — and composition_arc_apply blocks one step earlier for the same reason. Several tools now PROVEN (world_map_add_marker, composition_motif_bind_edit, catalog_get_book) show the signature in their earlier runs, which is the useful part: it is what a tool looks like on the way to being reachable, so it names a fixable class rather than a set of doomed tools.

The two mechanisms found today sit underneath it: the supplier is often not on the surface at all (D-THE-ONLY-SUPPLIER-OF-attr_value_id-IS-NEVER-ADVERTISED), and the repair that should name the supplier names nothing for 45 of 86 id-requiring tools (D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-THAT-IS-NOT-THERE).
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.method: Substring classification over recorded TOOL_CALL_RESULT contents; 'ok' counted as '"ok": true'. It cannot see calls whose result was never recorded, and 'other' failures are not broken down here. Stated so the denominator can be checked rather than trusted.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.fourth_instance: plan_bootstrap_apply, 2026-08-23: requires proposal_id, minted only by plan_bootstrap_propose. Apply advertised on 21 wire passes, propose on 0. The pair is named as a pair and the platform ships half of it.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.the_mechanism_named:
🔴 THE GUARANTEE STOPS AT DEPTH 1. R1 answerability forces onto the wire the tool whose declared vocabulary matches the request. NOTHING forces the tools THAT tool needs. A user names a goal, not an intermediate step, so a supplier is matched only by accident - and every one of the four instances is a tool the request's words do not describe:

    glossary_create_evidence (A)      <- glossary_get_entity (R)
    composition_arc_apply (A)         <- composition_arc_template_list (R)
    plan_bootstrap_apply (A)          <- plan_bootstrap_propose (A)
    composition_arc_template_get (R)  <- composition_arc_template_list (R)

THE TIERS REFUTE THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATION, which is why they are listed. 'The budget favours writes over reads' fits the first two pairs and fails the other two: plan_bootstrap_apply and plan_bootstrap_propose are BOTH Tier A, and composition_arc_template_get and _list are BOTH Tier R. So this is not a read/write asymmetry and it is not a tier rule. It is depth: the words select one tool, and its prerequisites are on their own.

That also names the fix precisely, as an extension of a mechanism that already exists rather than a new one: when R1 forces a tool, force the suppliers of its required opaque ids too. Still the owner's call - it is candidate (c) in D-THE-ID-REPAIR-SENTENCE-NAMES-A-TOOL-THAT-IS-NOT-THERE - but it is now a one-line statement of what is wrong rather than three alternatives.
D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-TH.depth_two:
🔴 IT GOES DEEPER THAN ONE HOP, measured 2026-08-23 on composition_reference_update (batch c-ref3, K=5, zero errored runs, called 5/5).

  composition_reference_update  requires reference_id  <- composition_find_references  ADVERTISED
  composition_find_references   requires entity_id     <- a glossary entity lookup     NEVER

From chat-service's own per-pass wire log across all 40 passes: composition_find_references on every pass; glossary_entity_id, glossary_get_entity and glossary_search on none.

The model does the right thing at every step and it does not help - it calls the write, is refused for reference_id, reaches for the correct supplier, and that supplier is refused for its own entity_id and ends in the loop-breaker. R1 matched exactly the tools the user's WORDS name (book_read, composition_reference_update, translation_patch_block).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX. The candidate 'when R1 forces a tool, force the suppliers of its required opaque ids too' must be TRANSITIVE, or this turn still fails one call later - level 1 was already on the wire here and the turn died at level 2. A one-hop fix would have looked correct on the other four instances and left this one exactly as broken.

D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.status: OPEN — measurement finding, 2026-08-23. It affects how six BLOCKED verdicts should be read.
D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.what:
A scenario with approve=None ends at the FIRST Tier-A card, whatever raised it. When that card belongs to some other tool, the tool under test never gets its turn — and the batch records 'called 0/5' as though the model declined it.

Six tools are blocked with exactly 'surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, suspended-on-card 5/5'. Read off their own raw evidence, the pending card is NEVER the tool under test:
    composition_entity_override_edit  <- kg_project_create (2), glossary_entity_set_attributes (3)
    tool_load                         <- kg_project_create, 5 of 5
    composition_generate              <- composition_arc_edit, book_chapter_save_draft,
                                         glossary_deep_research
(The other three sit in the multi-scenario `rebaseline` batch, where per-tool attribution of a pending card is not sound from the batch file alone — NOT counted as evidence here.)

This is the same shape that hid glossary_create_evidence's real cause earlier today: it was 'suspended 5/5' on a glossary_propose_entities card, and only once the harness was allowed to click did the tool get called 4/5 and fail on its actual defect — a required id with no supplier.

So 'called 0/5' under approve=None is not 'the model would not use this tool'. It is 'the model did not use this tool before something else asked permission', and those are different sentences.
D-A-NEVER-APPROVE-SCENARIO-MEASURES-REAC.what_it_does_not_mean:
It does not make approve=None wrong. A never-approve arm is the only way to see the Tier-A gate work, and it is one of the two user states this loop must run in. The error is reading a 'called 0/5' from that arm as a fact about the tool. The pair is the measurement: never-approve says whether the gate holds, approve says whether the tool is reachable.

It also does not license approving on a READ-intent scenario. tool_load keeps approve=None here, and that its read-only question raises a kg_project_create card on 5 of 5 runs is a finding about the product rather than an obstacle to clear.

D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICI.status: OPEN — measured 2026-08-23, batch c-r1-recheck, 30 runs, ZERO errored. It is the reason six tools are blocked, and no surfacing change can fix it.
D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICI.what:
Six tools were re-measured with the harness allowed to click cards (their old verdicts were decided by an unrelated tool's card). Every turn now completes and every scenario moves its store. All six are STILL called 0/5.

For each one the tool was advertised 5/5 AND answerable_tools picks it for its own prompt against the live 303-tool catalogue — verified per tool. The model had the right tool in front of it and chose a familiar sibling instead, on 5 of 5 runs, deterministically:

  composition_entity_override_edit -> glossary_entity_set_attributes  (writes the SHARED entity
                                      instead of a book-scoped override; entity_revisions moved 5/5)
  composition_generate             -> book_chapter_save_draft         (prompt says 'with the cowrite
                                      engine'; the tool declares 'cowrite')
  composition_glossary_build       -> glossary_adopt_standards
  glossary_propose_batch           -> glossary_adopt_standards
  plan_bootstrap_apply             -> plan_compile then a READ; never the apply
  tool_load                        -> glossary_book_ontology_read, then an unrequested write card
D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICI.the_decisive_case: glossary_propose_batch. answerable_tools returns EXACTLY ONE tool for its request — {glossary_propose_batch}, no competitor — and it was advertised 5/5. On 5 of 5 runs the model used glossary_adopt_standards, which the request does not match at all. The model passed over the only tool its own words selected in favour of one they did not. There is no surface fix for that: the surface was already correct.
D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICI.the_second_shape: composition_generate is the opposite problem and worth separating. R1 matched it AND book_chapter_create, book_chapter_save_draft, book_get_chapter, composition_get_prose — and forced all of them onto the wire, because R1 is deliberately not a ranking. So answerability delivered the right tool and its competitor together, and the choice fell back to the model, which took the familiar write. Guaranteeing a tool is VISIBLE and guaranteeing it is CHOSEN are different problems, and only the first is solved.
D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICI.why_it_matters: It re-classifies six of the nineteen blocked tools. Their prior reason — 'suspended on a card 5/5' — measured whether anything else asked permission first, not whether the tool is reachable. The real blocker is selection, and the candidate fixes are different in kind: disambiguating sibling descriptions, de-advertising a superseded/competing write when a more specific tool matches, or driving the choice from a rail. NOT MY CALL — recorded for the owner.
D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICI.correction_plan_bootstrap_apply:
🔴 plan_bootstrap_apply DOES NOT BELONG IN THIS ENTRY'S LIST and is left named here rather than quietly removed. It was filed as a selection failure ('plan_compile then a READ; never the apply'). Checked afterwards against chat-service's wire log: plan_bootstrap_apply was advertised on 21 passes and plan_bootstrap_propose - the ONLY producer of the proposal_id it requires - on ZERO. The model could not have applied the plan; the step that mints its input was never on its surface. That is D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-THE-MODEL-CANNOT-GET, not this defect.

The other five stand: for each of them the tool AND the sibling it lost to were both on the wire, and for glossary_propose_batch the tool was the only match its request had. The lesson from the misfiling is that a selection failure and a missing-supplier failure look identical at the point where you notice them - the tool was not called - and they are told apart only by asking whether every argument it needs was obtainable from that surface.
D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICI.completeness_variant:
A SEVENTH CASE, AND A DIFFERENT SHAPE: settings_provider_inventory, measured 2026-08-23. Asked 'What models can I use? Show me what my configured provider actually offers', the model called settings_list_models (18 registered models) 3-4 times per run and never settings_provider_inventory (69 provider models). R1 forced BOTH onto the wire.

The sibling did not answer the question WRONGLY - it answered HALF of it, correctly, and the model said so plainly ('registered in your account'). No false statement. So the failure is completeness, not mis-selection: a two-part request is satisfied by the part the first tool covers and the rest is dropped without a word.

It is also NOT the depth-1 supplier problem: settings_list_models returns the provider_credential_id that the inventory tool requires, on every row, and the model called it repeatedly. It held what it needed.

D-THE-NAME-REPAIR-WORKS-AND-ITS-BENEFIT-.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-23 (c-motiflink2, K=5). The mechanism is confirmed live; the improvement it was written to deliver is NOT, and the control says the model was already recovering.
D-THE-NAME-REPAIR-WORKS-AND-ITS-BENEFIT-.what:
_name_like_dropped_ids was added today so a refusal echoes back the NAMES the model passed where ids were required, instead of reporting them merely 'missing'. Its docstring cites composition_motif_link_edit over K=5: the model resolved both endpoints to names, the repair chain dropped them (correctly - they are not ids), the refusal said MISSING, and the model then called composition_motif_search WITH BLANK ARGUMENTS, twice, because the only thing it could have searched for had been deleted out of its own call.

THE MECHANISM IS CONFIRMED, verbatim from a live run: the refusal now reads '...You passed a NAME where an id is required (from_motif_id=\'Throwaway Loop Alpha Magogopa\', to_motif_id=\'Throwaway Loop Beta Magogopa\'). That is not missing - it is the wrong kind of value, and the name is what you search WITH...', followed by the runtime arming the supplier: '[SYSTEM] composition_motif_search is now available to you on this turn'. The model then searched with {"q": "Throwaway Loop Alpha Lotiguzo"} - the exact name.
D-THE-NAME-REPAIR-WORKS-AND-ITS-BENEFIT-.what_is_not_demonstrated:
🔴 THE CONTROL SAYS THE MODEL WAS ALREADY DOING THIS. The same scenario ran at 02:42 today as c2-motif, fourteen hours BEFORE the fix landed (e20a9ed80, 16:50). Its call sequences are indistinguishable from the post-fix run - composition_motif_link_edit -> composition_motif_search -> composition_motif_search, the same link_edit args - and every one of its searches already carried a query. So this run does not show the fix improving anything.

AND THE FAILING POPULATION IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE FROM THE EVIDENCE ON DISK. Reassembling TOOL_CALL_ARGS deltas per call id across every *-raw.json, composition_motif_search is called with no query in exactly one batch - rebaseline, 5 calls - and those come from the composition-motif-adopt scenario, whose prompt named no target, so searching the system scope with no query is the correct thing to do there and not this defect at all. The batch the docstring cites (batch19-v5) has no raw file on disk.

So: message correct, arming correct, benefit unmeasured. Recorded rather than counted as a win.
D-THE-NAME-REPAIR-WORKS-AND-ITS-BENEFIT-.method_note: My first pass at this said 'zero blank searches anywhere', including in rebaseline. That was wrong: TOOL_CALL_ARGS arrives as JSON DELTAS keyed by call id - the harness's own code comments say so - and I tested individual delta events instead of the reassembled call. Reassembling per call id found the rebaseline population immediately. A per-event test of a streamed argument is not a test of the argument.
D-THE-NAME-REPAIR-WORKS-AND-ITS-BENEFIT-.state_of_the_tool: composition_motif_link_edit stays BLOCKED and could not be concluded from this batch: 4 of 5 runs errored (2 ReadTimeout with zero calls, 2 upstream-error-after-a-call), which is the composition_motif_search transport stall, and the gate does not excuse a dirty turn even for a blocked verdict. Called 3/5 when the transport allowed it.

D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.status: FIXED 2026-08-23 (services/translation-service/app/migrate.py). Test test_the_version_backfill_can_run_twice.py, proven RED against the original statement on real Postgres. Service and worker both back up; catalogue 300 -> 312, PARTIAL cleared.
D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.what:
The version_num backfill claimed in its own comment to be 'Safe to re-run (idempotent - ROW_NUMBER is deterministic by created_at)'. ROW_NUMBER is deterministic only under a TOTAL ordering, and created_at is not one here: 13 (chapter_id, target_language) groups hold rows whose created_at match TO THE MICROSECOND, because the same statement wrote them. On a tie the order is arbitrary, so a re-run hands row B the number row A still holds.

It does not fail cleanly. The DDL runs in FastAPI lifespan, so the exception is a failed startup:
    UniqueViolationError: duplicate key ... constraint "idx_ct_version"
    ERROR:    Application startup failed. Exiting.
-> infra-translation-service-1 Restarting(3) -> ai-gateway 'provider translation list-tools failed -> PARTIAL' -> 300 tools federated instead of 312, and every translation tool off the wire.
D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.how_it_reached_this_loop: translation_job_control was carried as a BLOCKED tool on 'called 0/5'. It was never a tool defect and never a model failure: the tool was ABSENT FROM THE CATALOGUE because the service that owns it could not boot. Found by querying the live federated catalogue for the tool and noticing it was not there, then asking why - not from the eval evidence, which records exactly what a tool that does not exist looks like.
D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.the_fix:
Two changes, and the first alone still crashes.
  (1) ORDER BY created_at, id - a total order, so the assignment is identical on every run.
  (2) A two-phase renumber through the negative space. A single UPDATE that PERMUTES version numbers (A:1->2, B:2->1) violates the unique index MID-STATEMENT whatever the ordering, because a plain unique index is checked per row and cannot be deferred. Phase 1 parks every row at -version_num, emptying the positive space; phase 2 cannot then collide. Both ride one conn.execute, which asyncpg runs in an implicit transaction, so a phase-2 failure rolls phase 1 back rather than stranding rows negative - asserted by its own test.
D-TRANSLATION-SERVICE-COULD-NOT-BOOT-TWI.verified: Rebuilt and force-recreated both containers. translation-service Up (healthy), translation-worker Up, ai-gateway 'catalog: 312 tools / 10 providers' with no PARTIAL, and SELECT count(*) FROM chapter_translations WHERE version_num <= 0 returns 0.

D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-.status: OPEN - mechanism established 2026-08-23 by instrumenting R1 and reading the two call sites. It is the answer DQ-T31 was asking for.
D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-.what:
R1 answerability promises that a tool whose own declared vocabulary answers the request reaches the wire 'whatever the budget, the domain selection or the rail decided'. For an INTENT_GATED_SETUP_TOOL it cannot, and the reason is which CATALOG each advertise site is handed.

  line 8761, the ONE-OFF build:  _advertise_discovery_tools(_catalog_index(catalog), ...)
                                 -> the UNFILTERED catalog. R1 matches the gated tool here and
                                    adds it to tool_defs.
  line 3357, the PER-PASS build: cat_index = _catalog_index(discovery_catalog)
                                 -> the catalog AFTER filter_intent_gated_setup_tools. The tool
                                    is not in it, so answerable_tools cannot even match it, and
                                    this build REPLACES tool_defs on the first pass.

So the rescue happens exactly once, into a list that is then discarded, and every pass the model actually sees is built from a catalog the tool was removed from. Not a bug in either piece - the gate is doing its job and R1 is doing its job on the input it is given.
D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-.measured:
glossary_book_sync_apply, K=2, prompt 'Take the upstream changes - apply the standard updates to this book.' Its declared synonyms are 'apply the standard updates' and 'take the upstream changes' - the request is two of them verbatim, and against the live 303-tool catalogue answerable_tools returns EXACTLY {glossary_book_sync_apply}, no competitor.

chat-service's own logs, per turn:
    R1 answerability: request matches ['glossary_book_sync_apply']   <- once
    agent-surface advertised ... activated=34   sync_apply absent    <- every pass
and no 'NOT forced' line, because at the site that logged, the tool WAS in the index and WAS added. Batch c-syncapply: surfaced 0/2, called 0/2.

filter_intent_gated_setup_tools confirmed directly: with injected=[] or ['co_write'] the tool is removed; with ['glossary_shaping'] it survives.
D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-.what_it_answers:
DQ-T31 asks whether the world-setup gate should open on WHAT THE REQUEST ASKS FOR rather than on its vocabulary, and its recommendation is (a) - add a declaration arm, 'the rule R1 already applies at the advertise chokepoint'. This measurement shows that arm cannot be inherited for free: R1 runs at a chokepoint that no longer contains the tool. A declaration arm has to live in the GATE, before the catalog is narrowed, or the narrowing has to carry an exemption the way it already does for a pinned rail's step tools.

It also sharpens DQ-T3 (should the model be TOLD a gated tool exists). The tools are not merely unmentioned - they are unreachable by the one mechanism that exists to reach a tool by name.
D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-.superseded_for_this_tool_2026_08_24:
STILL TRUE AS STATED, AND NO LONGER glossary_book_sync_apply's BLOCKER. R1 genuinely cannot rescue an intent-gated tool — the per-pass build is handed the post-filter catalog — and whether a request that NAMES a tool should reach it anyway is still DQ-T31.

What was missing is the OTHER half of the same design. The gate's own principle is that 'guidance and capability move as ONE signal', and the signal is the glossary_shaping skill, injected when "glossary" is in enabled_skills. The FE sends enabled_skills on every message; the HARNESS never did, so every batch could only ever observe the gated case.

With the author's glossary skill pinned — which is what a person doing world work has — the tool is ADVERTISED 5 of 5, against 0 of 5 before. The gate is satisfied the way the product intends, not disabled.

D-A-FEDERATED-TOOL-DUPLICATED-BY-AN-ALWA.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-23. It explains one blocked tool and is worth a sweep for others.
D-A-FEDERATED-TOOL-DUPLICATED-BY-AN-ALWA.what:
registry_list_workflows (federated, Tier R) and workflow_list (consumer-local, dispatched inside stream_service) answer the same question with the same data - both return 12 workflows, same slugs, same slug/title/description shape. workflow_list is in the ALWAYS-ON CORE, so it is on every pass of every turn; the federated tool must win a hot-seed slot. A user's words cannot separate them.

Measured: asked 'What workflows are available to me?', the model called workflow_list 5/5 and gave a correct, complete answer. The gate's DATA bars pass on that evidence including 'answer is true'. The federated tool is unreachable on this surface by construction, and declares no superseded_by - the inverse of DQ-T2, which is about tools that declare deprecation and name no successor.
D-A-FEDERATED-TOOL-DUPLICATED-BY-AN-ALWA.worth_sweeping: The always-on core also carries tool_list, tool_load, confirm_action and web_search. Any federated tool that duplicates one of those is unreachable for the same reason and would look like a model failure in this loop's evidence. Not swept yet; recorded as owed.
D-A-FEDERATED-TOOL-DUPLICATED-BY-AN-ALWA.sweep_result:
SWEPT, and it is small. Comparing every federated tool's declared synonyms against the always-on consumer-local set across 315 tools, three overlaps:

  registry_list_workflows vs workflow_list  - 5 shared: workflows, list workflows, my workflows,
                                              what workflows, recipes  <- the blocked tool
  registry_get_workflow   vs workflow_load  - 1 shared: 'workflow steps'
  web_search              vs web_search     - SAME NAME, and BY DESIGN: the core sources its def from `catalog_index.get(name) or generic_frontend_tool_def(name)`, so a federated core tool is advertised from the catalogue's own definition. One tool, not a collision.

So the real population is TWO, both in the registry_* workflow family, and registry_get_workflow is the weaker case (one shared phrase, and the two may genuinely differ in scope).

🔴 METHOD LIMIT, STATED SO THE NUMBER IS NOT OVER-READ. The consumer-local tools do not publish a _meta.synonyms list to compare against - I supplied their vocabularies by hand from their code and descriptions. The registry_list_workflows result does not rest on that (its duplication was established by CALLING both and getting the same 12 slugs); the other two do. A hand-written comparison set can miss a duplicate whose wording I did not think of, so THREE is a lower bound.

D-A-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-ONLY-THE-AUTHOR-CA.what:
op=create refuses without budget_usd and pause_after_each_unit. Neither is an id and neither has a supplier tool by nature: they are decisions only the AUTHOR can make - how much money to spend, and whether to pause between units. The model is correctly forbidden from inventing them ('Do NOT guess a value'), no tool can provide them, and nothing in the refusal tells it to ASK THE USER. The turn has no legal move.

Distinct from the missing-supplier family, where a supplier exists and is off the wire, and from the sibling family, where another tool wins. Here the right next action is a question, and the platform's whole repair vocabulary is about finding values rather than requesting them.
D-A-REQUIRED-ARGUMENT-ONLY-THE-AUTHOR-CA.recommendation_for_owner: Either give such arguments a server-side default (a budget ceiling from settings, pause=false), or make the refusal say 'ask the author for X' rather than 'do not guess a value'. NOT MY CALL. It pairs with DQ-T35, which recommends a server-resolved default for composition_generate's model_ref on the same reasoning.
