D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.ANSWERED_2026_08_24_BY_READING_NOT_RUNNI:
THE MISSING LOG LINE IS EXPLAINED, and it cost nothing to find once I did what I had written down: enumerate the paths a tool result can take, instead of running the batch again.

THERE ARE FOUR mcp_execute_tool CALL SITES. Two are in the main loop (7126 and its helpers). TWO ARE IN `resume_stream_response` - 11067 and 11198 - and that second one is where an APPROVED Tier-A tool actually executes.

The resume dispatch is a far thinner path:
    _ok = bool(envelope.get('success'))
    _tool_payload = envelope.get('result') if _ok else {'error': envelope.get('error')}
    working.append({...})
    _chunk = {..., 'ok': _ok, 'error': envelope.get('error')}
    instrument.stamp_tool_call(_chunk, source=instrument.SOURCE_TOOL, ...)
No arming. No cross-wire correction. No repeat-breaker. That `_chunk` is exactly where the chat_messages.tool_calls record's `ok=false, source=tool` and the NOT_A_DERIVATIVE text come from - so the evidence I kept re-reading was written by the very path that has no arming.

AND IT EXPLAINS THE SPLIT IN THE DIAGNOSTIC PERFECTLY. Every tool that DID log is Tier R - composition_list_outline, composition_list_canon_rules - and runs in the main loop. composition_entity_override_edit is Tier A: it suspends for approval and executes on resume. I instrumented the main loop and measured a tool that never goes through it.

🔴 THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THIS SESSION THE RESUME PATH HAS BEEN THE ANSWER. Earlier: 'R1 answerability was inert on every resumed turn' because _emit_chat_turn was called without request_text. The general fact is worth more than either instance: THE RESUME PATH IS SYSTEMATICALLY MISSING THE MAIN LOOP'S GUARDS, and every guard added to the main loop should be asked of it.
D-A-DOMAIN-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-AND-ARMS.fix_shape_not_shipped:
Arming at the resume dispatch is necessary and NOT sufficient, and the reason is in the code's own comments. After dispatching, resume re-enters _stream_with_tools and RE-DERIVES ITS SURFACE FROM SCRATCH - 'a resume re-derives its surface from scratch (WS-3)'. `susp.pinned_step_tools` exists precisely to carry an exemption across that boundary, 'because dropping the exemption here would strand a rail at its FIRST confirm gate'.

So the shape is: resolve the tools named in the resumed tool's refusal, and carry them across the re-derivation the way pinned_step_tools already carries a rail's steps.

BUT THE MEASURED WITHHOLDING IS domain_not_selected AND hot_seed, and filter_intent_gated_setup_tools - where pinned_step_tools is applied - is the INTENT GATE, a different filter. Pinning there may exempt the wrong one. Which of the three filters must honour a refusal-named tool is the question to answer BEFORE writing this, and answering it means reading the surface builder, not running another batch.

NOT SHIPPED. It is a change to how a resumed turn chooses its surface, and I have already learned this cycle what happens when I change surface selection on a hunch: c-override8, where suppressing one backfill starved the model of the only id it had.

D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.status: OPEN - found 2026-08-24 from chat_messages.withheld_tools, 5 of 5 turns.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.what:
composition_entity_override_edit's refusal names composition_list_derivatives. That tool is WITHHELD from the turn for two independent reasons, recorded by the platform itself:

    domain_not_selected | domain not in this turn's hot set (book, glossary, knowledge, story)
    hot_seed            | did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)

Five of five turns, both reasons. The turn's hot set does not include composition's divergence domain at all, and even if it did the tool did not fit the seed budget.

So the instruction 'Call composition_list_derivatives' is issued into a turn that selected a different set of domains entirely. Arming exists to rescue exactly this - but arming is a mid-turn correction layered on top of a selection made at turn start, and the measurement says the rescue did not happen.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.why_it_matters_beyond_this_tool: It is P1-SURFACE's invariant reaching a case R1 cannot cover. `answerable_tools` forces a tool onto the wire when the AUTHOR'S REQUEST matches its declared synonyms. Here the tool is needed because of a REFUSAL - the platform's own words, mid-turn - and no author phrasing would ever have named it. A surface chosen from the request cannot anticipate the tools the request's failure will require.
D-A-REFUSAL-CAN-ONLY-ARM-WHAT-SURVIVED-D.recommendation_for_owner:
Two shapes, both wider than one tool. (a) Treat a tool named in a refusal as budget-exempt for the remainder of the turn, the way D-RAIL-NEXT-STEP-EXEMPT already treats a rail's next step - the precedent exists and is narrow. (b) Let a declared emitter pull its consumer's domain into the hot set: composition_entity_override_edit already declares project_id <- composition_list_derivatives, so the platform knows the pair before the turn starts.

(b) is the one I would price first: it acts at SELECTION time rather than patching the selection afterwards, and it uses a declaration that already exists and is already verified.

D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-24 against the deployed matcher and the live 315-tool catalogue. It is a RECOMMENDATION for DQ-T41, not a decision.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.what:
composition_generate's blocked reason calls this a genuine tie — 'R1 is deliberately not a ranking, so when several tools declare the same words they all arrive and the choice falls back to the model.' Measured, the tie is MANUFACTURED by the matcher, twice over.

1. NORMALISATION COLLAPSES DISTINCT DECLARATIONS. `_answer_norm` strips articles, so three tools that declared DIFFERENT phrases become identical:
       composition_generate      'write chapter'      -> 'write chapter'   len 13
       book_chapter_create       'write a chapter'    -> 'write chapter'   len 13
       book_chapter_save_draft   'write the chapter'  -> 'write chapter'   len 13
   The article is load-bearing and the authors used it that way: 'write A chapter' is the CREATE tool, 'write THE chapter' is the edit-existing tool. Stripping it destroys the distinction they encoded, and manufactures an exact three-way tie at length 13.

2. THE LOOP BREAKS ON THE FIRST MATCH, SO THE DISCRIMINATING TERM IS DISCARDED. composition_generate declares NINE synonyms and the request matches TWO of them:
       index 2  'write chapter'   matched by 3 tools in the catalogue
       index 5  'cowrite'         matched by EXACTLY 1 tool in 315   <- never reaches the ranker
   `for syn in synonyms: ... break` stops at index 2. So a tool's contribution is whichever synonym happens to sit earliest in its list — declaration ORDER decides the match, which no author would expect to matter — and the one term that identifies this tool uniquely, in a prompt that says 'with the cowrite engine' outright, is thrown away before ranking begins.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.recommendation_for_DQ_T41:
DQ-T41 asks what precedence should break an exact tie. On this evidence the more useful question is why the ranker is being handed a tie at all.

RANK BY SPECIFICITY, NOT LENGTH. The current key is `-len(normalised_synonym)`, and length is a poor proxy for how much a phrase identifies a tool: 'cowrite' (7 chars) is matched by 1 tool in 315; 'write chapter' (13 chars) by 3. A count of how many catalogue tools match the same normalised synonym is computable from the catalogue at the same moment, needs no new declaration, and is exactly the signal a tie-break wants.

It resolves the other recorded instances the same way and without a domain-vs-generic rule: jobs_cancel's 'stop the translation' would still tie translation_job_control on length and lose on specificity, because the domain tool's vocabulary is matched by fewer tools. A precedence rule stated as 'longer synonym wins' resolves NEITHER instance, since both are exact ties.

PREREQUISITE, and it is small: collect a tool's BEST matching synonym rather than its first. As written the ranker cannot see 'cowrite' at all, so no tie-break — length, specificity or otherwise — can use it.

NOT SHIPPED. This is a change to how EVERY request selects its surface, and it is DQ-T41's own question. The measurement is the contribution; the decision is the owner's.
D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-.what_it_does_not_explain: It does not explain why the model then picks book_chapter_save_draft over the others once all five are on the wire — that is a choice among tools it can see, and this loop's rule is that a surface finding does not become a model finding without its own measurement. What is now known is that the surface handed the model a tie it did not have to.

D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-24. The strongest instance of P5 arm (b) in the loop, and the remedies are owner decisions.
D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.what:
composition_glossary_build runs a whole pipeline — its first line says so: 'You do NOT pick per-entity tools: this ONE tool runs the whole pipeline — it plans WHAT to build (a worklist), builds each entity in its own focused step, files them as review drafts, then projects them into the graph and proposes their relationships.'

The model runs glossary_extract_entities_from_doc -> glossary_propose_entities instead, on 5 of 5 runs, and SUCCEEDS at the surface goal: glossary_entities moves 5/5. What the author loses is not the cast — they get that — but the worklist, the deep profiles, the review drafts and the proposed relationships.

🔴 AND THE ANSWERABILITY LAYER IS DOING EVERYTHING IT CAN. Measured against the deployed matcher and the live catalogue for this exact prompt:
       R1 forces: ['composition_glossary_build']   — EXACTLY ONE TOOL, via 'build the knowledge graph' (21 chars)
   Neither competitor declares anything that matches the request: glossary_extract_entities_from_doc's vocabulary is all 'extract entities from a document' / 'parse my notes', and glossary_propose_entities' is all 'create a new entity' / 'bulk create entities'. They are on the wire because the GLOSSARY DOMAIN is in the hot set, not because anything decided they answer this request.

So this is not a tie, not a ranking problem, and not a surfacing problem. The platform favours the right tool as strongly as its design permits — sole forced tool — and the model chooses the parts it can also see.
D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.it_corrects_the_recorded_numbers: 🔴 The blocked reason on file says 'answerable_tools ranks this tool FIRST for its own prompt (synonym length 23, against kg_build 21)'. Measured now: the match is 21 characters, not 23, and kg_build is NOT in the answerable set at all — the set has exactly one member. The old numbers made this look like a near-run ranking; it is not close, and that makes the finding STRONGER rather than weaker.
D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-.why_the_obvious_remedies_are_not_mine:
SUPPRESS THE PARTS. They arrive by domain seeding, and the glossary domain is correctly hot for a glossary request. Removing them would break every job that legitimately needs one entity created — the tools are not wrong, they are wrong FOR THIS REQUEST, and nothing on the surface knows which request it is looking at.

GIVE IT A WORKFLOW. The platform already has the mechanism and states it in the system prompt: 'If the user's request matches one of these, call workflow_load FIRST and follow its steps IN ORDER — do NOT improvise your own tool sequence for a job a workflow already covers.' That is this failure named exactly. But no workflow covers this job: `glossary-bootstrap` is ONTOLOGY setup ('Set up a book's world categories' — list standards, adopt, confirm, read back), not entity building. Checked in loreweave_agent_registry.workflows rather than assumed.

So when no workflow matches, the directive PERMITS improvising — and the model did exactly what the platform allows. Authoring a workflow changes what every user sees in workflow_list, which is a product surface, not a lint.

RECOMMENDATION, in order of what I would price first: (1) a one-step workflow whose step IS composition_glossary_build, because the rail mechanism already exists and is designed for precisely 'a job a workflow already covers'; (2) nothing else — a description warning is already there, in the tool's FIRST LINE, and did not prevent it on 5 of 5 runs, which is the bound this loop has now measured twice.

D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-24. A general property of the answerability layer, with registry_list_workflows as its measured instance.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.what:
`answerable_tools` ranks over the FEDERATED catalogue. Consumer-local meta tools are advertised alongside federated ones but are not in it — `_CONSUMER_LOCAL_META_TOOLS` in stream_service holds find_tools, tool_list, tool_load, workflow_list, workflow_load and run_subagent, each with its own tool def built in chat-service rather than fetched from the gateway.

So R1 cannot see them. It cannot rank one, cannot deprioritise one, and cannot know that one DUPLICATES a federated tool it is busy forcing onto the wire. A consumer-local tool that overlaps a federated one wins unconditionally.

MEASURED, for 'What workflows are available to me?' against the deployed matcher and the live catalogue:
       R1 forces: ['registry_list_workflows']      <- the SOLE forced tool
       workflow_list:  NOT IN THE FEDERATED CATALOGUE
and the model calls workflow_list on 5 of 5 runs. Both return count=12 with identical slugs, so the author is answered correctly — which is why this cost nothing visible and stayed invisible.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.it_corrects_the_recorded_reason: 🔴 The blocked reason says workflow_list is 'in the ALWAYS-ON CORE'. It is not: ALWAYS_ON_CORE_NAMES, read from the deployed service, is exactly (tool_list, tool_load, confirm_action, web_search). workflow_list is advertised by a different route — its def lives in workflow_runner.WORKFLOW_LIST_TOOL and it is dispatched inside stream_service. The CONCLUSION was right (it is always reachable and R1 cannot outrank it) and the mechanism named was wrong, which matters because the fix differs: nothing about ALWAYS_ON_CORE_NAMES would change this.
D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOC.recommendation_for_owner:
TWO LEVELS, and I would price the first.

1. THIS TOOL. registry_list_workflows declares no `superseded_by` — the inverse of DQ-T2's complaint about 55 tools that declare deprecation and name no successor. Here is a tool superseded IN PRACTICE that says nothing. Marking it `visibility='legacy', superseded_by='workflow_list'` is the mechanism the kit already provides, and it would remove it from discovery on both federation surfaces. NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE, which is why it is the owner's: a legacy tool is excluded from the agent's discoverable set, so it can never again be PROVEN by a live run — the honest outcome is that it leaves the denominator as deprecated rather than sitting blocked forever.

2. THE CLASS. `answerable_tools` should rank over the tools actually ADVERTISED, not only the federated catalogue, or its ranking stays blind to every consumer-local competitor. That is a change to the matcher's input rather than its rules, and it would let R1 at least SEE the duplication it is currently ranking against.

D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.status: OPEN - measured 2026-08-24 across THREE tools. The clearest statement of P5 arm (b) the loop has, and it bounds what answerability can ever fix.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.what:
`answerable_tools` forces a tool onto the wire when the request matches its declared vocabulary. It is ADDITIVE by design — 'deliberately not a ranking' — so it can put the right tool in front of the model and cannot take a wrong one away. The competitors arrive by DOMAIN SEEDING, which answerability never consults.

MEASURED ON THREE TOOLS, each time with R1 forcing the correct tool as the SOLE member of the answerable set:

  composition_glossary_build   forced alone via 'build the knowledge graph' (21).
      Model ran glossary_extract_entities_from_doc -> glossary_propose_entities, 5/5.
      Neither competitor declares anything matching the request.
  registry_list_workflows      forced alone. Its twin workflow_list is CONSUMER-LOCAL and not
      in the federated catalogue at all, so R1 cannot even see it. Model used the twin 5/5.
  translation_job_control      forced alone via 'stop translation' (16) on the domain
      question. Model called jobs_cancel + jobs_summary, 5/5, and called the tool under test
      ZERO times.

So the answerability layer is doing everything its design permits in all three, and losing in all three. The failure is not that the right tool is missing — it is present, forced, and alone in the set — but that the wrong ones are equally present and more familiar.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.the_attempt_that_failed:
🔴 I REWORDED translation_job_control's PROMPT TO ITS OWN DOMAIN QUESTION AND IT DID NOT WORK. Recorded because the reasoning was sound and the result refutes it.

The scenario read 'Cancel job — stop translation for this book's running translation job.' Measured, that phrasing makes the tool match BOTH 'cancel job' (10) and 'stop translation' (16), and the matcher BREAKS on the first hit — so it contributed 10 and tied jobs_cancel exactly, while its longer exclusive match was discarded. The prompt front-loaded the generic tie-maker.

'Stop the translation for this book.' forces translation_job_control ALONE — jobs_cancel matches nothing. Batch c-tjc3, K=5, zero errored runs:
        surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, suspended 3/5
        every run: jobs_cancel + jobs_summary
and jobs_cancel then failed on 'missing required argument(s): [job_id]' — the model could not even complete the tool it preferred.

THE HYPOTHESIS WAS THAT AN UNAMBIGUOUS ANSWERABLE SET WOULD DECIDE THE CHOICE. It does not. The precedent I was following — settings_provider_inventory, where asking only the tool's own question moved it from 0/5 to 4/5 — does not generalise: there the sibling ANSWERED THE OTHER HALF of a two-part question, so removing that half removed the competition. Here the sibling answers the SAME question, badly, and stays on the wire regardless of what is asked.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.what_it_means_for_DQ_T41:
It narrows the decision. A precedence rule — by specificity, by domain, however stated — changes which tools are FORCED. On this evidence that is not the binding constraint for these three, because the right tool was already forced alone and lost anyway.

A rule that only reorders the answerable set would not have moved any of them. What would is a rule that lets a forced tool SUPPRESS a domain-seeded sibling for that turn — which is a much larger claim about the surface, and squarely the owner's.
D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REM.OVERSTATED_2026_08_24:
🔴 OVERSTATED, and retracted in part the same day. It cited THREE tools as "R1 forcing the correct tool as the SOLE member of the answerable set" and losing anyway. Re-measured against the LIVE catalogue rather than the frozen snapshot I had been using: only registry_list_workflows is actually forced alone. composition_glossary_build forces FOUR (itself, kg_add_nodes, kg_build, kg_graph_query) and translation_job_control forces BOTH itself and jobs_cancel.

WHAT STILL STANDS: for composition_glossary_build the two tools the model ACTUALLY used (glossary_extract_entities_from_doc, glossary_propose_entities) are not in the answerable set, so a domain-seeded competitor did beat a forced tool there. And R1 IS additive by construction — that is a property of the code, not of these measurements. What is withdrawn is the claim that three separate tools were each forced ALONE and lost, which was the strength of the argument. See D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZEN-CATALOGUE.

D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZE.status: FOUND AND RETRACTED 2026-08-24, same day. The instrument was stale; three of my own 'corrections' corrected records that were RIGHT.
D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZE.what:
In cycle 3 I needed a catalogue to run `answerable_tools` against, and built one from contracts/agent-runtime-baseline/tools-list.snapshot.json — a FROZEN baseline, as its path says. I then reused that same file for five cycles without once asking whether it matched the running system.

Compared against the live catalogue (315 tools in both, no additions or removals — which is exactly why the staleness was invisible):
    jobs_cancel   snapshot: ['cancel job','stop job','abort job','kill job',
                             'stop a running job','cancel my task']
                  LIVE:     ...the same SIX, PLUS 'stop the translation', 'stop it',
                             'cancel it', 'stop that one'
    propose_edit  snapshot: no synonyms
                  LIVE:     ['show me the change','suggest an edit','propose an edit',
                             'rewrite this','rewrite the selection','insert at my cursor']
The second is my OWN change from cycle 1 of this session, which I then failed to see.
D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZE.what_it_falsified_of_mine:
THREE CORRECTIONS I PUBLISHED ARE THEMSELVES WRONG, and the records they corrected were right:

1. translation_job_control (cycle 6). I wrote that my earlier move note 'cites synonyms that do not exist' and that 'the 16-character tie I recorded does not happen'. It does. Live: 'Stop the translation for this book.' forces BOTH, translation_job_control via 'stop translation' (16) and jobs_cancel via 'stop the translation' (16 after the article is stripped). DQ-T41's second instance is REAL, and the generic tool did colonise the domain tool's vocabulary exactly as first recorded.

2. composition_glossary_build (cycle 4). I wrote 'R1 forces EXACTLY ONE tool' and 'kg_build is NOT in the answerable set at all'. Live it forces FOUR — composition_glossary_build, kg_add_nodes, kg_build, kg_graph_query — so the original note's 'length 23 against kg_build 21' was describing something real and my correction was not.

3. propose_edit (cycle 7). I read 'synonyms: None' off the frontend def and concluded R1 forces nothing for it. Live, R1 forces propose_edit and nothing else. Cycle 1's measurement was right.

WHAT SURVIVES, re-checked against the live catalogue rather than assumed:
  * the break-on-first-match mechanism (D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-NOT-GENUINE). composition_generate's live synonyms are identical to the snapshot's, the 5-tool set reproduces, and translation_job_control still contributes 'cancel job' (10) while its best match is 16. The mechanism is real on both tools.
  * registry_list_workflows: R1 forces it alone, and workflow_list is genuinely not in the federated catalogue. Unaffected.
  * the c-tjc3 RUN ITSELF: K=5, called 0/5, jobs_cancel every run. Live data, still valid — but its FRAMING was wrong. I built that arm believing R1 would force translation_job_control alone. It forces both. So the arm never tested what I said it tested, and 'an unambiguous answerable set does not decide the choice' is NOT supported by it.
  * D-R1-FORCING-ADDS-THE-RIGHT-TOOL-AND-REMOVES-NO-WRONG-ONE is OVERSTATED: of the three tools I cited as 'forced alone and lost', only registry_list_workflows actually was.
D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZE.why_it_was_invisible:
The snapshot and the live catalogue have the SAME 315 tools, with no additions and no removals. Every sanity check I would naturally run — does the tool exist, is the count right, does the name resolve — passes. Only the _meta of two tools had drifted, and one of those drifts was my own edit earlier the same session.

The file is named `contracts/agent-runtime-baseline/tools-list.snapshot.json`. It says BASELINE and it says SNAPSHOT. I read the path when I wrote the loader and used it anyway because it was the convenient shape.

THE RULE I ALREADY HAD AND DID NOT APPLY: verify the deployed thing matches the source before diagnosing anything from its behaviour. I applied it to service images four times this session — checking each rebuild carried my change — and never once to the catalogue I was measuring WITH.
D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZE.the_fix: Measurements now read the LIVE catalogue: knowledge_client.get_tool_definitions inside chat-service, written to /tmp/live.json. The frozen snapshot has a legitimate use — it is a baseline for detecting drift — and none at all as the input to a question about what the system does NOW.

D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.status: FIXED in the harness 2026-08-24; the live re-measure is what proves it.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.what:
INTENT_GATED_SETUP_TOOLS — glossary_adopt_standards, glossary_propose_kinds, glossary_plan, glossary_propose_batch, glossary_book_sync_apply — are filtered out of the TURN CATALOG itself unless the turn carries world-setup intent. The signal is the `glossary_shaping` skill, which skill_registry injects when `"glossary" in enabled_skills`.

The gate is deliberate and was measured: 'the co-writer proactively rebuilt a newcomer's ontology on a plain "write a chapter 1" turn: three prior fixes failed because hot-seed + find_tools exclusions don't cover tool_load, which loads ANY catalog name.' Its stated principle is that guidance and capability move as ONE signal.

🔴 THE FRONTEND SENDS enabled_skills ON EVERY MESSAGE. This harness never did — `enabled_skills` appears nowhere in scripts/toolloop — so every batch it has ever run observed only the GATED half of that signal. Those five tools could not be measured at all: not because the product cannot reach them, but because the instrument could not construct the state the product requires.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.why_this_is_the_instrument_and_not_the_p:
glossary_book_sync_apply's recorded reason says 'THE INTENT GATE REMOVES IT FROM THE CATALOG, AND R1 CANNOT PUT IT BACK ... whether that is correct is DQ-T31'. Both halves stand: R1 genuinely cannot rescue an intent-gated tool, and whether a request that NAMES a tool should reach it anyway is still the owner's question.

What was missing is the OTHER half of the same design — that the tool IS reachable when the author signals world work, which is exactly what pinning the glossary skill means. A harness that can only ever send the gated case can only ever report the gate.
D-THE-HARNESS-CANNOT-PIN-A-SKILL-SO-FIVE.the_fix:
`enabled_skills` is now a scenario field, threaded through send_turn into the message body — the same field the FE sends. Additive: a scenario that omits it behaves exactly as before, so no existing batch changes meaning.

It does NOT decide DQ-T31 and does not soften the gate. It lets a scenario say which skills the author has pinned, which is a property of the AUTHOR's session that the harness was simply unable to express.

D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.status: OPEN - named 2026-08-24. It became visible only once the intent gate was satisfied.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.what:
glossary_book_sync_apply applies a DIFF between a book's adopted standards and the system standards. With the gate satisfied and the tool advertised 5 of 5, the model does exactly the right thing on every run: calls glossary_book_sync_available first, finds the diff EMPTY, and tells the author so — 'there are currently no upstream changes to apply. Your story bible is up to date with the latest standards.'

called 0/5 is therefore CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, not a failure. There was nothing to apply.

The scenario's own seed_assert says as much and always did: 'Standards adopted, nothing upstream changed since.' The fixture was never built to create a divergence — which nobody could see while the gate kept the tool off the wire entirely.
D-BOOK-SYNC-HAS-NOTHING-TO-APPLY-AND-A-D.why_a_divergence_cannot_be_seeded_within:
Probed directly on a throwaway book, torn down after: adopting a NARROW slice ({genres:['universal'], kinds:['character']}) and then calling glossary_book_sync_available returns {"updates": []}. A partial adopt does not leave the rest pending, so the obvious cheap divergence does not exist.

What WOULD create one is the SYSTEM standards changing after the book adopted — and system standards are shared across every book and every user of this deployment. Writing them to make a test pass is a larger violation than the dogfood book this loop already refuses to touch: it would change what every other author's sync sees. I am not doing it.

RECOMMENDATION: a test-only way to seed a divergence scoped to ONE book — a system-standard version pinned per book, or a fixture hook that records the book as adopted at an older revision. Until then this tool cannot be exercised, and that is a property of what the fixture can safely build rather than of the tool.

D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.status: CAUSE NAMED and FIXED 2026-08-24; live proof pending.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.retracts:
🔴 THIS RETRACTS THE BLOCKED REASON I WROTE FOR composition_authoring_run_manage. It said 'CALLED 5/5 AND BLOCKED ON A run_id NOTHING CAN LOOK UP ... NO TOOL LISTS OR RETURNS AN EXISTING RUN'. That is FALSE on two counts, both checkable statically:
  (1) composition_package_tree ALREADY returns a `.runs/` block — the 5 most recent plan runs for the book, each with id/status/mode, via PlanRunsRepo.list_for_book. The model CALLED package_tree on 5 of 5 runs. I wrote 'nothing lists a run' about a surface that lists them.
  (2) composition_authoring_run_list takes book_id ALONE, so authoring runs are listable too.
I reasoned from the required-args table (every plan_* tool takes run_id, only plan_propose_spec does not) and concluded no reader existed, without reading what the readers RETURN. A required-arg census answers 'what must I pass', never 'what comes back'.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.what_actually_happened:
The durable gate task SURVIVES teardown (mcp_gate_tasks), so the model's real arguments are still on disk. They are very nearly RIGHT:
    book_id              01a02fb6-f41c-...   the fixture book, CORRECT
    budget_usd           "5"                 the prompt said 5 dollars, CORRECT
    pause_after_each_unit true               the prompt asked to pause, CORRECT
    plan_run_id          01a02fb6-f4b2-...   a REAL UUIDv7, not a placeholder
So this is NOT the D-UNDECLARED-REF/model_ref class ('default' as an id). Every validator in _execute_authoring_run_create passes on this payload, which leaves exactly one raise: svc.create -> plan_runs.get_for_book(book_id, plan_run_id) -> None -> LookupError('plan run not found') -> HTTPException(400, {'code':'action_error'}) with NO message.

AND THE MODEL'S OWN EXPLANATION IS A CONFABULATION. Run 1 answered 'the plan_run_id I used was actually the book_id itself'. The stored payload shows it was not. A model's account of its own failure is not evidence.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.theory:
A CROSS-WIRE, not an invention. The same id 01a02fb6-f4b2 was also sent as `book_id` to composition_package_tree, which failed 'not found or not accessible'. One id in two different id-shaped slots is a cross-wire; and a UUIDv7 stamped ~150ms after the fixture book cannot be fabricated by a model — the timestamp is in the id. So f4b2 is a REAL id provisioning created.

  H1  f4b2 is the fixture's project_id (composition_work, minted right after the book).
      Predicts BOTH observations: not a book -> package_tree 'not accessible'; not a plan run ->       LookupError. Store.before confirms a composition_work row exists.
  H2  f4b2 is the SEEDED plan run's id. REFUTED by the 400 itself: the seed_assert proves a       compiled plan run exists ON THIS BOOK, and get_for_book filters on nothing but (id,       book_id), so if f4b2 were it the create would have SUCCEEDED.
  H3  a third provisioning artifact.
H1 is the one the evidence supports; H3 stays open until the ids are compared.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.refuted_if: The seeded plan run's id EQUALS what the model sent (then the fault is in book scoping, not a cross-wire), or the model's plan_run_id differs from the fixture's project_id (then it is H3 and the source must be named before anything is fixed).
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.why_this_was_not_decidable_before: THE INSTRUMENT DISCARDED THE ONLY IDS THAT INTERPRET THE PAYLOAD. provision.py records `fx.project_id` and `fx.seeded` (every seed step's result), and fe_runner's batch writer picks fields explicitly — it keeps book_id and drops BOTH. So a batch can show a cross-wired id and contain nothing to say what that id IS. That is why this tool got a confident, wrong blocked reason. Recording them is a prerequisite for the measurement, not a convenience.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.measured_outcome:
BOTH OF MY HYPOTHESES WERE REFUTED BY THE MEASUREMENT, and recording that is the point of having written them down first.
  H1 the project_id — REFUTED. H2 the seeded plan run — REFUTED.
The id is the fixture's CHAPTER_ID: the editor context the turn carries. Identified on 2 of 2 runs of batch c-authrun4-diag, by an instrument built for the purpose (fe_runner.seed_ids), against the payload recovered from mcp_gate_tasks.

ONE CROSS-WIRE, TWO VICTIMS, AND THE SECOND IS WHY IT IS SELF-SEALING:
  composition_package_tree      book_id      = the chapter id -> 'not found or not accessible'
  composition_authoring_run_manage plan_run_id = the chapter id -> LookupError -> bare 400
package_tree is the tool that RETURNS the real plan run id (`runs.recent`). The cross-wire breaks the lookup that would have corrected it, so the model can never recover inside the turn.
D-AUTHORING-RUN-CREATE-APPROVE-THEN-FAIL.two_named_causes:
C2 — THE DROP EXISTS AND COULD NOT SEE THIS ARGUMENT. `_inject_context_ids` iterates over exactly ('book_id','chapter_id','project_id'), so a context id landing in an argument called anything else is never examined. Verified against the DEPLOYED function: given {book_id: BOOK, plan_run_id: CHAPTER} it returned plan_run_id UNTOUCHED, while the same function given package_tree's {book_id: CHAPTER} correctly SUBSTITUTED the real book. The mechanism was not weak here, it was absent — and the absence is invisible because those three names cover most tools. FIXED: _drop_crosswired_foreign_ids, same evidence standard (exact match against an id this turn published under another name), same emitter narrowing, DROP only and never substitute.

D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.status: OPEN — named 2026-08-24. Terminates in DQ-T42, an owner decision. NOT fixed.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.what:
composition_generate validates its SCENE target at propose (the node must exist and be in the gated Work's project) and does not validate its CHAPTER target at all. Measured over MCP: a chapter_id that does not exist mints a confirm_token; so does a chapter belonging to a different book, in both directions. The author is shown a cost-bearing approval card for a generation that cannot succeed.

It is APPROVE-THEN-FAIL, not a cross-book write: the payload carries the GATED project's book_id, the chapter path resolves scenes by scenes_for_chapter(project_id, chapter_id), and the persist targets that same book_id — so a foreign chapter fails at confirm. Read from the code rather than confirmed, because confirming spends.

The behaviour is DELIBERATE and documented in the source: 'The CHAPTER target is validated at confirm by the engine (it needs book-service to resolve the chapter sort/plan).'
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.why_i_did_not_just_fix_it:
Because the fix cannot be made without choosing a failure mode, and the choice is not mine.

composition-service holds no authoritative chapter table: outline_node.chapter_id covers only OUTLINED chapters, and a chapter with no scenes is normal and legitimate, so a local check would refuse valid work. Existence therefore requires book-service. The obvious helper, get_chapter_sort_orders, is explicitly NOT book-scoped ('the caller MUST have verified book ownership first') and returns {} on ANY failure — so a guard built on it would fail OPEN, which is the shape this loop has already filed as a defect twice.

So the real question is what the most expensive tool on the platform does while book-service is unreachable, and both answers cost something.
D-GENERATE-MINTS-A-COST-BEARING-CARD-FOR.dq_t42_recommendation:
DQ-T42 — should composition_generate verify the CHAPTER target at propose, and what happens when book-service cannot answer?

MY RECOMMENDATION, and it is a recommendation: verify at propose against a BOOK-SCOPED book-service route (get_draft is scoped by URL: /v1/books/{book_id}/chapters/{chapter_id}), and FAIL CLOSED with a refusal that says the target could not be VERIFIED rather than that it does not exist. Reasons: an unverifiable target during an outage is exactly when a bogus spend is hardest for an author to understand; the refusal costs nothing while the alternative costs money; and 'degrade must surface unverified' is already this platform's rule elsewhere. The cost is real and should be stated plainly: during a book-service outage no chapter generation could be proposed at all.

THE OWNER DECIDES. I am not making this change to unblock a tool.

DQ-T1.question: What is `entity_lifecycle_ledger` for, and what should write it? Options seen, none chosen: (a) every status transition (approve/retire/reject via glossary_propose_curation) appends a row, making the ledger the audit trail its columns describe; (b) it is delete/restore-only by design and the column set is aspirational; (c) it is superseded by entity_revisions and should be dropped.
DQ-T1.evidence: Measured 2026-08-13. The table exists with an append-only trigger guard (`entity_lifecycle_ledger_append_only`) and columns op, prior_status, new_status, actor_type, actor_id, reason — the exact vocabulary of a curation status change. It holds THREE rows, all from 2026-08-11, all op='deleted'/'restored', and all with prior_status and new_status NULL. A repo-wide search for 'lifecycle_ledger' finds NOTHING in source, and the only database function referencing it is the append-only guard. Four entities were moved draft -> active live in this cycle and the ledger gained no rows. So it is a table with a guard, no writer, and a column set that describes a transition nobody records. Whether curation SHOULD write it is a product decision about what the audit trail is for, not something measurement can settle.
DQ-T1.recommendation: RECOMMEND (a) - every status transition appends. Not because the ledger is used, but because somebody paid for an append-only TRIGGER on it: that is a deliberate integrity guarantee, and a guarded table holding three rows from a single day is the shape that later gets read as an audit trail it never was. (c) drop-it is the honest alternative and is cheaper; what makes it the wrong DEFAULT is that the columns (op, prior_status, new_status, actor_type, actor_id, reason) already describe the curation transition exactly, so the intent is not in doubt. Decide (c) only after checking for readers - if anything reads it today, (c) is a silent capability loss.

DQ-T5.question: How does a NEW book get its first glossary entity? Options seen, none chosen: (a) let a refusal UNLOCK the tool it names for the rest of the turn, the way a pinned rail's step tools are already exempted from the intent gate; (b) make the router inject glossary_shaping on prose like 'set up my book, adopt the standard lore categories', which it does not today; (c) let glossary_ontology_upsert create a kind that is actually usable (with a display attribute), so the non-gated path works end to end; (d) bootstrap a default ontology with the book, the way a knowledge project is already bootstrapped 197ms after creation (OBS-T17).
DQ-T5.evidence: Measured live 2026-08-13 across sessions 019ffa85, 019ffa92 and 019ffa96 on a throwaway book, with every branch tried. A fresh book has no kinds, so glossary_propose_entities refuses. Its remedy, glossary_adopt_standards, is intent-gated and was recorded WITHHELD at stage=intent_gate in the same turn as the refusal that named it - and stayed withheld even on the explicit prose 'Set up my book - adopt the standard lore categories for it'. The non-gated alternative, glossary_ontology_upsert, DOES create the kind (confirmed in the store) but the kind has no display attribute, so the propose is correctly refused with 'refusing to create a nameless entity'; adding a name attribute through the same tool returned ok and changed nothing - the retry produced a byte-identical refusal. DQ-T6.question: Should the hot-seed budget be allowed to advertise a domain's WRITE tools while dropping its primary READ tool? NOTE: this is about what a plain request LANDS ON, not about reachability — a budget-dropped tool is still reachable via tool_list -> tool_load, proven 2026-08-13. Options seen, none chosen: (a) reserve a slot for each domain's read tools before any write is seeded; (b) spend the budget by RELEVANCE to the turn's request rather than by domain order; (c) raise or scale the 2000-token hot-seed budget; (d) treat a read/write imbalance in a seeded domain as a loud failure rather than silently seeding whatever fits.
DQ-T6.evidence: Measured 2026-08-13 across four attempts on two surfaces. Asked in plain prose to read a chapter, the model never called book_read; it called book_chapter_save_draft. On the BOOK STUDIO surface the runtime recorded book_read withheld with reason 'did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)', and the book tools it DID advertise were book_chapter_save_draft and book_update_details — both writes. On the universal surface book_read was withheld as domain_not_selected and then token_budget, and never advertised at all. This is the causal explanation for three separate write-for-read substitutions recorded the same day (OBS-T16, OBS-T22, OBS-T28), one of which overwrote a real chapter's prose with 'This is a test.' and was only recoverable because the write had snapshotted first. The tool itself is fine — called directly it returns faithful data. Which way to fix the budget is a product decision about how the hot set is spent; measurement can show the imbalance but not the intended policy. SECOND INSTANCE, 2026-08-13 (cycle 22, session 019ffaf4): asked to suggest arc structures for a named BOOK, the turn's hot domain was selected as `knowledge`, and composition_arc_suggest was withheld at stage=domain_not_selected with reason 'domain not in this turn's hot set (knowledge)'. The model then called load_skill('composition') TEN times without reaching any composition tool. So the pattern is not book-service-specific: on both services the surfacing layer, not the tool, is what stops a plain request from being served — once by spending the hot-seed budget on writes (book_read), once by selecting a domain the request never mentioned. THIRD AND SHARPEST MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-13 (cycle 25): retested on the EDITOR surface — the one stream_service documents as seeding 'glossary + composition + book tools hot' — a single turn advertised only 4 of composition's 107 tools, withheld 49 more with 'did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)', and withheld the rest as domain_not_selected. All four tools this loop needed (arc_suggest, arc_template_get, get_outline_node, get_derivative_context) were in the budget-dropped set, and each is verified correct under direct exercise. So the constraint is the 2000-token hot-seed budget itself: on the surface built for authoring, a 107-tool domain gets 4 slots, and which 4 is decided by fit rather than by what the author asked for. CORRECTION 2026-08-13: a budget-dropped tool is NOT unreachable — asked to load it by name, the model runs tool_load and calls it successfully, which is the designed lazy-tail path. Four composition tools and book_read were all recorded BLOCKED on this misreading and are now PROVEN. What remains real, and is what this DQ is about, is the CONSEQUENCE of the seeding choice: on the editor surface the budget advertised book_chapter_save_draft and book_update_details while dropping book_read, and a model asked four separate times to READ reached for a WRITE instead — once overwriting a real chapter's prose. The tools were reachable; nothing in the turn told the model so.
DQ-T6.recommendation: RECOMMEND (b) - spend the hot-seed budget by RELEVANCE to the request, not by domain order. The platform has already committed to this principle one stage later: R1 answerability exists to force a tool whose declared vocabulary answers the request onto the wire 'whatever the budget, the domain selection or the rail decided'. (b) applies that same rule at seeding time, so it removes the need for the rescue instead of adding a second mechanism beside it. (a) fixes the measured case and not the class; (c) raising the budget buys time and changes nothing structural.
DQ-T6.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.
DQ-T6.evidence_2026_08_23:
FOUR NEW INSTANCES, AND THEY DO NOT SUPPORT THIS DQ'S FRAMING - recorded because a DQ strengthened with the wrong evidence is worse than one left alone.

This DQ asks whether the hot-seed budget should advertise a domain's WRITE tools while dropping its primary READ. Four tools blocked on 2026-08-23 all failed because a required id's supplier was on no pass of the wire, which looks like the same thing. It is not. Two of the four pairs are Tier A consumer <- Tier R supplier and fit the framing; the other two are Tier A <- Tier A (plan_bootstrap_apply <- plan_bootstrap_propose) and Tier R <- Tier R (composition_arc_template_get <- composition_arc_template_list), and neither is a read losing to a write.

What the four share is DEPTH, not tier: the request's words select one tool and nothing carries its prerequisites. See D-THE-LOOPS-DOMINANT-FAILURE-IS-AN-ID-THE-MODEL-CANNOT-GET. The recommendation on this DQ - spend the budget by relevance rather than domain order - is unchanged and still stands on its own 2026-08-13 measurement (book_read withheld for budget while two book WRITES were advertised).

DQ-T30.question: When a rail is DONE, what re-reads the data? A completed rail correctly stops driving, and the model then answers data questions from conversation memory — which goes stale the moment anything changes outside the chat. MEASURED 2026-08-13: with two rules in the store, a re-ask returned 'one rule' (the count from the earlier turn); told a rule had been added, the model claimed 'I have checked your consistency rules again' with ZERO tool calls and INVENTED a plausible rule paraphrased from the chapter prose in place of the real one. Options seen, none chosen: (a) a rail step whose tool is a READ never latches done, so a re-ask always re-drives; (b) a freshness window — a read step older than N minutes is re-actionable; (c) a turn-level rule that a question naming stored data must be answered from a tool call in THIS turn, independent of any rail. (c) is the general fix and the most expensive.
DQ-T30.evidence: Session 019ff929, book 019ff8f5, 2026-08-13 14:0x-14:2x. Store: 2 active canon_rule rows ('Sat khi luon tieu hao tuoi tho — magic always costs lifespan', 'The Obsidian Trench never appears on two maps at once'). Turn A (rail drove): tool called, answer correct. Turn B (canon-check now 3/3, 'guards held but no actionable step'): no tool call, answered 'one rule'. Turn C: no tool call, answered with the real first rule plus a FABRICATED second one, 'The world is constantly rewriting itself through shifting geography'. Note this is NOT the same gap as D-FJ-18, which is now fixed and covers the first ask; it is what happens after that ask has already succeeded.
DQ-T30.decision: ANSWERED 2026-08-14 by the owner: option (c) — a question naming stored data must be answered from a tool call in THIS turn, independent of any rail. The general fix and the most expensive, chosen over the two rail-scoped options.
DQ-T30.shipped: (c) built as the turn-level guard (5093177a1). MEASURING it exposed the real mechanism — a completed rail REMOVES the answering read (e133167d2). Both are load-bearing: guard alone 0/3, guard+reclaim 3/3.
DQ-T30.recommendation: RECOMMEND: rail completion suppresses WRITES only, never READS. A finished rail correctly stops driving, but the measured consequence is the model answering data questions from conversation memory - a stale count, then 'I have checked your consistency rules again' with ZERO tool calls and an INVENTED rule. Re-reading is not duplicated work: it IS the freshness the author asked for, and there is nothing to double-apply. The codebase already carries this reasoning for the rail gate's reclaimed reads; this is the same rule at turn scope.
DQ-T30.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.

DQ-T31.question: Should the world-setup intent gate open on WHAT THE REQUEST ASKS FOR rather than on its vocabulary? Options seen, none chosen: (a) add a declaration arm, as the consent check now has — if the request's own words match a gated setup tool's declared synonyms, treat the turn as setup intent; (b) widen the glossary_shaping skill router's phrase list (fixes these sentences, leaves the class); (c) leave it — N5a-FULL is a deliberate over-reach guard and being hard to open is the point, in which case the withheld tools must at least be VISIBLE as withheld, which is DQ-T3 and needs the model to call tool_list.
DQ-T31.evidence:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, two prompts for the same tool, K=3 each.
  v1 'Set up several kinds and attributes at once for this book's ONTOLOGY — I want to do it in one batch': intent_gate withheld 0 tools. Gate OPEN.
  v2 'Set these up together in one batch for this book: a kind called Faction with an attribute Allegiance, and a kind called Artifact with an attribute Origin': intent_gate withheld 4 — glossary_propose_batch, glossary_plan, glossary_propose_kinds, glossary_book_sync_apply. Gate SHUT.
The CONCRETE request — the one that names the exact kinds to create, and is world-setup by definition — is the one denied the tools. The vague one, which the model could not act on (it correctly asked WHICH kinds), got them.
CONSEQUENCE, not inferred: with the batch tool invisible, the model reached for glossary_adopt_standards on 3/3 and suspended on ITS card — adopting SYSTEM standards, which would not create Faction or Artifact at all. It substituted a different tool with different semantics rather than saying it could not do what was asked.
DQ-T31.why_the_DQ_T3_stamp_did_not_help: The stamp is emitted by tool_list/tool_load and the model called NEITHER on any run. This is the D-LAZY-TAIL-UNUSED interaction in full: a tool is withheld, the notice that would explain it lives behind a discovery call the model does not make, and the model substitutes. It is also the first NON-VOID instance of the DQ-T3 condition — three earlier attempts all found the gate open.
DQ-T31.status: OPEN — product decision, recorded per the RUNBOOK rather than answered.
DQ-T31.recommendation: RECOMMEND (a) - add a DECLARATION arm to the intent gate: if the request's own words match a gated setup tool's declared synonyms, the turn is setup intent. It is the rule R1 answerability already applies at the advertise chokepoint, so it introduces no new concept, and it fixes the class rather than the two measured sentences. The evidence is decisive against (b): two prompts asking for the SAME tool differ only in phrasing, and the gate opens for one while withholding four tools for the other. Choosing (c) obliges the withheld tools to at least be stated, which is DQ-T3.

DQ-T32.question: Should answerability match a declared synonym as a CONTIGUOUS phrase, or should the matcher tolerate pronoun substitution and interposed words? DQ-T32.evidence: Batch 12's natural experiment: perfect correlation between 'a declared synonym appears verbatim' and 'the tool was surfaced', 1/5 -> 5/5 once the declarations were widened. Every original miss was a pronoun substitution or an interposed word, never a different meaning.
DQ-T32.why_it_is_a_decision: _synonym_pattern's word-boundary work exists because 'cat' matched inside 'category' and cost a live run. Relaxing the matcher trades precision for recall across all 315 tools, and the CONSENT check now depends on answerability too — a read-only turn sets a standing write grant aside — so a widening changes consent behaviour, not just surfacing. Option (a) is shipped and working; (b) and (c) need measuring against the live catalogue.
DQ-T32.status: OPEN — recorded per the RUNBOOK rather than answered.
DQ-T32.sharpened_2026_08_21: composition_motif_bind_edit surfaced 0/5 on a CLEAN arm — the tool never reached the wire. DQ-T32.measured_2026_08_23:
THE WHOLE CORPUS, MEASURED. 194 unique (tool, measured-turn) pairs across every scenario on disk, run through the platform's own answerable_tools:
  RECALL   185/194 (95%) — the tool under test IS answerable on its own prompt.
  SET SIZE mean 1.8, median 1, max 6, against ANSWERABLE_MAX=8. Three turns match nothing.
So the matcher is not flooding the wire, and there is headroom under the cap for a more permissive rule — which is the thing option (b) would spend.

THE SHARPENED CASE IS HALF-CLOSED, AND THAT IS THE ARGUMENT. composition_motif_bind_edit's 'Bind Emberfall Vein to the opening arc' now matches, because a bare 'bind' was added to its declarations — option (a) working exactly as advertised, and it is the ONLY answerable tool on that turn, so nothing was lost to imprecision. One phrasing fixed, three left, on one tool. That is option (a)'s cost curve measured rather than asserted.

THE 9 MISSES ARE NOT ONE POPULATION, and only the first group is this question's:
  3  composition_motif_bind_edit — a contiguous synonym split by the object's NAME. Option (b)      (in-order subsequence with a bounded gap) is aimed exactly here.
  2  tool_load — CORRECTLY unmatched. Answerability keys on the AUTHOR's words and no author asks      to load a tool schema. Relaxing the matcher must not 'fix' these.
  4  propose_edit, memory_recall_entity, translation_coverage, glossary_propose_batch — plain      declaration gaps, which option (a) closes and option (b) would not.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST MEASUREMENT, recorded because it nearly became the recommendation: I first counted 'a short synonym matched a tool that is not the tool under test' and got 110 of 122, which reads as catastrophic imprecision. It is not a precision measure at all — answerability returns a SET, and the co-matches were composition_motif_search on motif prompts (the SUPPLIER, which is desirable) and world_map_list on 'List the maps' (simply correct). Set size is the honest proxy, and it is 1.8.
DQ-T32.recommendation_2026_08_23:
OPTION (a) FOR NOW, WITH ONE NAMED EXCEPTION, and re-open only if the exception recurs. Recall is already 95% and the mean set is 1.8 of a possible 8, so a relaxation buys at most 3 of 194 turns and spends precision across all 315 tools — and the CONSENT check now reads answerability too, so it would move consent behaviour, not just surfacing. That is a poor trade at this margin.

The exception is worth deciding separately: a synonym whose words are split by the OBJECT'S OWN NAME ('attach pattern to chapter' vs 'attach the pattern called X to the chapter') is not a different intent and never will be. If option (b) is taken, bound it to that shape — an in-order subsequence over the synonym's words with a gap cap — rather than a general relaxation, and measure set size again before shipping. Option (c) (rarity weighting) is not supported by any measurement here and should not be taken on intuition.

Owner's call either way; this is a recommendation, not a decision.
DQ-T32.third_instance_2026_08_23:

The SECOND sentence is the one that disambiguates — it asks for live inventory in plain words — and measured against the real matcher it is answerable by ZERO tools. DQ-T33.blocked_by: a product decision, so recorded and not asked
DQ-T33.question: When a turn ends with no user-visible text, should the service surface the last TOOL error to the author rather than leaving the reply blank?
DQ-T33.why_it_is_a_product_decision: The tool's own message is often the most useful sentence available ('composition_arc_get is missing required argument(s): [node_id], and this tool does not declare which side supplies them — so do NOT guess a value'), and showing it is reporting what happened, not inventing prose. But it exposes internal tool vocabulary in the author's chat, which is a voice-and-surface decision this loop must not make unilaterally. The alternative — a generic apology — IS invented prose, and three prose interventions were measured and refuted on 2026-08-14.
DQ-T33.what_shipped_meanwhile: Only the RECORDING is fixed: a silent turn is now stored outcome=failed instead of completed, so the 21 measured cases stop counting as successes. The author still sees a blank reply when it happens.
DQ-T33.sharpened_by: The root cause is now known: the turn is not empty, it contains a stray `<tool_call|>` delimiter. So the product question is narrower than 'what do we show for an empty turn' — it is 'the model emitted a malformed call; do we retry it, surface the last tool error, or say something generic?'
DQ-T33.recommendation: RECOMMEND yes - surface the last tool error when the turn produces no text. A blank reply is indistinguishable to the author from a hung request, and the service already HAS the error it is withholding. 🔴 THE evidence FIELD OF THIS DQ IS EMPTY. This recommendation rests on the question as posed plus adjacent findings in this loop (a dead call recorded as a silent success; a silent turn is not a completion) - not on a measurement of this behaviour. Measure it before deciding.
DQ-T33.recommendation_status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the owner decides. Added 2026-08-23.
DQ-T33.mechanism_now_known_2026_08_24:
THE DECISION HAS A MECHANISM UNDER IT NOW, WHICH SPLITS IT IN TWO. It was posed as 'what does the service show the author when a turn says nothing' - one question, answerable only in the abstract because the silence had no known cause. It now has one:

The model abandons the structured tool-call channel and emits ONLY the closing control token `<tool_call|>`. There is no call to salvage. The hold that would have caught it is keyed on the OPENING token, a different string, so the delimiter flushes into the reasoning channel and the pass ends as an ordinary 'stopped without a tool call'. `_is_bare_toolcall_marker_only` now names that state, with 14 tests and a proven-RED falsifier.

SO THERE ARE TWO SEPARABLE QUESTIONS, and only the second is really a product one:

  (a) WHAT THE SERVICE DOES. The model's INTENT was a tool call - it emitted the delimiter for one. Retrying that pass is ordinary engineering on a degenerate generation, not a choice about what the assistant may say. It is cost-bearing (one more provider call) and it changes turn behaviour, which is why it is not shipped unilaterally - but if (a) is answered 'retry', (b) may never fire in practice.

  (b) WHAT THE AUTHOR SEES if the retry also comes back degenerate. This is the original question and it stays the owner's. The constraint the loop already recorded still binds: putting words in the assistant's mouth here would be this loop's own 'prose is not the lever' mistake in service code.

RECOMMENDATION: answer (a) first. It is cheap, it is measurable (the log line now counts the population), and it is the half that could unblock settings_provider_inventory - which fails 1 run in 5 on precisely this.

Only THREE are required: composition_generate, composition_library_translate, kg_build_wiki. composition_generate is the outlier on the one tool where the cost of getting it wrong is highest, and both measured failure modes (placeholder, then abandonment) vanish if the runtime supplies the model it already knows.

DQ-T36.blocked_by: a product decision about how the turn's tool catalogue is built
DQ-T36.question: What decides which tools are advertised on a turn, and should a tool the request NAMES be guaranteed a place?
DQ-T36.measured: 30 of the 65 blocked tools were never advertised (surfaced 0/N across clean runs, zero transport errors). THREE hypotheses are RETIRED BY MEASUREMENT and must not be re-run: (1) RANKING — world_map_update_marker scores #1 of 315 and world_map_update_region #2 for their own measured prompts, using the shipped scorer offline, and both surfaced 0/5. (2) TIER/SCOPE/FAMILY — settings_model_set_active, _set_favorite and _update surfaced 0/5 in the same batch where settings_update_profile surfaced 5/5 and carded 5/5; same account scope, same tier, same family. (3) BATCH COMPOSITION — memory_timeline surfaced 5/5 inside a 5-scenario batch, then 0/5 alone, 0/5 alone again, then 0/5 inside a 5-scenario batch.
DQ-T36.why_it_is_not_merely_a_reachability_ques: A budget-dropped tool is still reachable via tool_list -> tool_load, and the model DOES use that path (registry_get_workflow: 'I do not have access to its internal instructions without loading it first'). What is not survivable is the OTHER outcome: when the missing tool is a WRITE, the turn reports the write as DONE. world_map_update_marker 5/5, kg_triage_resolve 5/5 (which rendered the post-resolution state to make it convincing), plan_keep_material 4/5 with zero tool calls, world_map_remove_region 1/5. Same condition produced honest refusals elsewhere, so the model is not uniformly at fault and the surface is the variable.
DQ-T36.options_seen_none_chosen: (a) reserve a slot for any tool whose declared synonyms match the request, so a named tool is never silently absent; (b) leave selection as-is and make the ABSENCE explicit to the model, the way DQ-T3's withheld-stamp already does for gated tools; (c) leave both and rely on tool_list -> tool_load, accepting that a write tool may be missing from a write turn.
DQ-T36.note: Option (c) is the status quo and is measured to produce false success. It is listed so the decision is made rather than defaulted into.
DQ-T36.cycle: P1-SURFACE, cycle 1 of the resolution loop — 25 tools.
DQ-T36.measured_2026_08_22_cycle_2:
THE MECHANISM IS NOW MEASURED, not hypothesised, using the platform's own functions offline (scripts/toolloop/hotseed_starvation_probe.py imports _budget_names_impl / hot_tool_names / surface_hot_domains rather than reimplementing them). A turn's advertised set is: the hot seed (a surface's hot DOMAINS, filtered to a HOT_SEED_TOKEN_BUDGET of 2000 tokens) UNION the session's activated_tools UNION core/frontend UNION whatever answerable_tools forces on. On the studio surface that is 120 candidates keeping 21.

THE BUDGET IS THE CULLING MECHANISM AND IT SYSTEMATICALLY CUTS SUPPLIERS. It orders reads by ASCENDING schema size, which is inversely correlated with how central a tool is — tool_surface.py already says so in its own words: 'a primary read takes filters and documents them, while a peripheral one takes a single id ... Fitting the MOST tools is not fitting the RIGHT ones.' Measured casualties: composition_motif_search 900 tok, composition_arc_template_list 356, composition_authoring_run_list 223 — all STARVED, all list/search tools, all the supplier of a blocked tool.

THE SECOND HALF OF THE QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED IN THE CODE. A tool the request NAMES *is* guaranteed a place: answerable_tools forces a synonym match onto the wire 'whatever the budget' (tool_surface.py), capped at ANSWERABLE_MAX=8. So the guarantee exists — what was missing is that it is keyed on the AUTHOR's words, and a SUPPLIER is named by the REFUSAL rather than by the author. That gap is what cycle 2 fixed reactively (D-REFUSAL-NAMES-A-TOOL-THE-TURN-CANNOT-SEE).

THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE IS NOW STALE. It says 30 of 65 blocked tools were never advertised. Swept 2026-08-22 across the 48 still-blocked: 46 are ANSWERABLE against their own recorded prompts, so their 'surfaced 0/N' predates cycle 1's 37 declaration widenings and has not been re-measured. The two that are not answerable are propose_edit (a real gap — it declares no synonyms) and tool_load (NOT a gap — no author asks to load a tool schema).
DQ-T36.recommendation_2026_08_22: Do NOT widen ALWAYS_HOT_READS to rescue the starved suppliers, and do not raise HOT_SEED_TOKEN_BUDGET. Both spend the authoring surface's prefix on every turn to fix a case that arises only after a refusal, and tool_surface.py's own docstring asks for evidence rather than intuition before adding to that set. The reactive arming shipped in cycle 2 costs nothing on turns that do not need it and is measured working live. What IS worth deciding: whether a required argument may ship with an EMPTY description (105 of 467 do, 75 of them id-shaped) — because that, not the budget, is what leaves a refusal with no tool to name.

DQ-T40.blocked_by: a change to the loop's own evidence standard, which is not mine to make
DQ-T40.question: Should gate.py excuse the LIVE clean bar when every errored run is a NAMED transport defect and the tool was demonstrably exercised on the clean runs?
DQ-T40.measured: composition_motif_link_edit: 35 runs across four arms, 17 transport failures (~49%), 18 clean runs on which the tool was called 3/5, 4/5 and 5/5 with its supplier armed and reached. Thirteen hypotheses for the transport failure tested and refuted; it is not load, not eviction, not my probe contention, not service state, not turn count, not schema size, not encoding, not context pressure. At 49% a transport-clean K=5 has ~3% probability, so re-running is not a path.
DQ-T40.why_it_is_not_mine: Loosening the gate in the very cycle whose completion it blocks is indistinguishable from making the evidence fit, and this run has already caught itself twice wording past a bar. The bar's current strictness is also defensible: a turn that died upstream is genuinely no evidence about the tool, and the rule exists so a platform failure is never recorded as a tool's property.
DQ-T40.recommendation: Do NOT widen the excused set generally. If anything, add a THIRD terminal state — something like `unmeasurable`, requiring a registered defect id, the arm count, and the clean-run evidence — so a tool blocked by a platform failure leaves the queue with its situation described rather than being silently reclassified as `blocked`, which would read as a property of the tool. Until then P3 stays at 6/7 and the loop moves on to the next problem.
DQ-T40.superseded_2026_08_23:
🔴 WITHDRAW THIS QUESTION. Its premise was 'thirteen hypotheses refuted, the cause is not findable, and at ~49% a transport-clean K=5 has ~3% probability, so re-running is not a path'. Every clause of that was wrong, and wrong in a way worth recording.

TWO NAMED CAUSES, both found by looking at what the turn DID rather than at how often it failed:
  1. THE FIXTURE HAD BEEN DEAD FOR TWO DAYS. Both motifs were archived by a sibling scenario and      never restored — unrecreatable (the unique index has no status predicate), unresolvable      (get_by_codes is active-only), and asserting green (the seed_assert had no status filter).
  2. THE REFUSAL DELETED THE ANSWER. With the fixture repaired, all five runs read      link_edit -> motif_search -> motif_search -> dead. The model resolved both endpoints to      NAMES, the whitespace arm dropped them correctly, and the refusal reported them MISSING —      so the follow-up search had nothing to search for and went out blank, twice.

AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT 'REFUTED' CONTENTION COULD NOT SEE CONTENTION. `ps aux` under Git Bash does not enumerate native Windows processes; two runners were live at one point while it reported none. That hypothesis was never actually tested, and it was recorded as refuted.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which outlives this tool: a failure RATE is not a diagnosis, and a long list of refuted hypotheses is not evidence that the cause is unfindable — it is evidence about where I had been looking. The rate said 'flaky platform'; the call SEQUENCE said 'unwinnable turn', and it was in every run the whole time. Do NOT add an `unmeasurable` terminal state on the strength of a rate: it would have absorbed this tool and closed both defects unfound.

DQ-T41.blocked_by: a product decision about which tool wins an ambiguous request, which is not mine
DQ-T41.question: When two tools tie on synonym match, should a DOMAIN-SPECIFIC tool take precedence over a GENERIC one — and should that precedence be a declared field or an implicit ranking rule?
DQ-T41.measured:
composition_generate: surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, ZERO errors. On its own prompt five tools are answerable and THREE tie at synonym length 13 — book_chapter_create, book_chapter_save_draft, composition_generate. The domain tool declares 'write chapter'; the generics declare 'write the chapter' and 'write chapter prose'. No precedence exists, so the tie is broken arbitrarily.

The worst outcome is not the miss. When the tie breaks toward book_chapter_save_draft the model supplies prose it wrote ITSELF (D-GROUNDED-REQUEST-ANSWERED-WITH-UNGROUNDED-PROSE), so an ambiguous ranking silently converts a grounded request into an ungrounded one.
DQ-T41.why_it_is_not_mine: Precedence changes which tool wins for EVERY ambiguous request, not just this one — it is a product decision about what the platform should do when a user's words fit two tools, and it can only be evaluated against the whole catalogue. Cycle 2's arming cannot help here and that is structural: arming is REACTIVE and fires on a refusal, so a tool the model never CALLS never produces one.
DQ-T41.recommendation:
DECLARE it, do not infer it. Today's lesson on settings_list_models is that two attempts to make a declaration louder were measured and refuted, and what worked was changing the MECHANISM. Lengthening composition_generate's synonym is the same refuted move. A `_meta.specificity` (or an explicit `supersedes: [tool]`) makes the intended winner reviewable and testable, where an implicit 'domain beats generic' heuristic is a rule nobody can see in the declaration and that silently reorders 315 tools.

DO NOT ship a tie-break without measuring the OTHER side: any rule that promotes composition_generate here demotes something else elsewhere, and this loop has no measurement of that population. Recall before precision — the same order that applies to a lint.
DQ-T41.scope_measured_2026_08_23:
HOW MUCH THIS DECISION BUYS, measured so it can be weighed rather than assumed. Across P5-SIBLING-WINS' five blocked tools, exactly ONE is a genuine synonym tie - composition_generate, 3-way at length 13. The other four have a clear winner on the platform's own ranking (override_edit 21 vs 15, glossary_build 23 vs 21, registry_list_workflows the only member, provider_inventory 11 vs 6) and the model chose otherwise anyway - in three of them a tool that is not in the answerable set at all.

So declaring precedence fixes 1 of 5 here. That does NOT argue against it: the recommendation stands, because an arbitrary tie-break silently converts a grounded request into an ungrounded one (the model supplies prose it wrote itself). It argues against expecting this cluster to clear as a result.
DQ-T41.second_instance_2026_08_23:
A SHARPER CASE THAN composition_generate's, and it changes what the decision has to cover. There the three tied tools are peers. Here a GENERIC tool ties a DOMAIN tool by borrowing its words:

    'Cancel that job.'                     translation_job_control 10  |  jobs_cancel 10
    'Stop the translation for this book.'  translation_job_control 16  |  jobs_cancel 16

jobs_cancel declares 'stop the translation', 'cancel it', 'stop that one', 'cancel my task'. Its 'stop the translation' is translation_job_control's 'stop translation' with an article added - so the generic tool ties the specific one EXACTLY in the phrasing where the user names the domain.

A precedence rule stated as 'domain-specific beats generic' would resolve both instances. A rule stated as 'longer synonym wins' would resolve NEITHER, because both are exact ties - which is worth knowing before the mechanism is chosen.
DQ-T41.third_instance_and_a_recommendation_2026:
MEASURED: THE TIES THIS QUESTION IS ABOUT ARE MANUFACTURED BY THE MATCHER. See D-THE-ANSWERABILITY-TIE-IS-MANUFACTURED-NOT-GENUINE. Two mechanisms, both measured against the deployed code:
  * _answer_norm strips articles, so composition_generate's 'write chapter', book_chapter_create's 'write A chapter' and book_chapter_save_draft's 'write THE chapter' all become the same 13-character string — an exact three-way tie among tools that declared different things, and the article was how their authors told create from edit.
  * the match loop BREAKS on a tool's first matching synonym, so composition_generate's 'cowrite' — matched by exactly 1 tool in 315, and named outright in the prompt — never reaches the ranker at all.

RECOMMENDATION: rank by SPECIFICITY rather than LENGTH — how many catalogue tools match the same normalised synonym. It is computable from the catalogue at that moment, needs no new declaration, and resolves all three recorded instances, including jobs_cancel vs translation_job_control, WITHOUT needing a domain-beats-generic rule. A rule stated as 'longer synonym wins' resolves none of them, because every instance is an exact tie.

PREREQUISITE: collect a tool's BEST matching synonym instead of its first, or no tie-break can see the discriminating term.
